exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In phase changes: Solid $\right arrow$ Liquid is Melting ($\text{X}$); Liquid $\right arrow$ Gas is Boiling/Vaporization ($\text{Y}$); Gas $\right arrow$ Solid is Deposit i on ($\text{Z}$); Liquid $\right arrow$ Solid is Freezing ($\text{M}$).

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
If $K_{c1}$ and $K_{c2}$ are the equilibrium constants for the two reactions:
1. $\text{XeF}_6 (g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeOF}_4 (g) + 2\text{HF}(g) \quad K_{c1}$
2. $\text{XeF}_4 (g) + \text{XeF}_6 (g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeOF}_4 (g) + \text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2 (g) \quad K_{c2}$

What is the equilibrium constant for the reaction:
$$\text{XeF}_4 (g) + 2\text{HF}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2 (g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Reversing reaction (1) gives an equilibrium constant $1/K_{c1}$. Adding the reversed reaction (1) to reaction (2) yields the target reaction. When chemical equations are added, their equilibrium constants are multiplied: $$K = K_{c2} \times \frac{1}{K_{c1}} = \frac{K_{c2}}{K_{c1}}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: How is the reaction quotient ($Q_c$) related to equilibrium constant ($K_{eq}$)?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The reaction quotient $Q_c$ has the same mathematical expression as the equilibrium constant $K_c$ using non-equilibrium concentrations. Exactly when a system reaches dynamic chemical equilibrium, $Q_c = K_c$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which statement best explains why alcohols generally have higher boiling points than alkanes with similar molecular mass?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Alcohols possess polar hydroxyl ($-OH$) functional groups with highly electronegative oxygen atoms, enabling strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding that requires substantially higher thermal energy to separate.

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
Given the following compounds, what would be the correct decreasing order of boiling point?:
I. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$
II. $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}$
III. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{COOH}$
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: All three compounds are structural isomers of hexanoic acid ($C_6H_{12}O_2$). The unbranched straight chain (II) provides the greatest surface area and van der Waals contact, followed by the mono-branched isomer (I), while the highly branched isomer (III) is most compact with the lowest surface area. Thus: $\text{II} > \text{I} > \text{III}$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following describes a general method for synthesizing esters from carboxylic acids and alcohols, emphasizing reaction conditions and equilibrium?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Fischer esterification involves heating a carboxylic acid and alcohol under reflux in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, which acts as an acid catalyst and a dehydrating agent to drive the equilibrium toward ester formation.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which evaluation correctly describe physical and chemical properties of oils?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Plant and vegetable oils are triglycerides rich in unsaturated fatty acids with double bonds (rendering them liquid at room temperature). They undergo catalytic hydrogenation (addition of $H_2$) to form saturated solid fats like margarine.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Why tricarboxylic acids have higher boiling points than monocarboxylic acids?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Tricarboxylic acids contain three carboxyl groups ($-COOH$), facilitating an extensive 3D network of multiple intermolecular hydrogen bonds as well as higher molecular mass.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: In a redox reaction: $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl} \long right arrow \text{MnCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the roles of the reactants?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The oxidation state of manganese drops from $+4$ in $\text{MnO}_2$ to $+2$ in $\text{MnCl}_2$ (reduction). Hence, $\text{MnO}_2$ is the oxidizing agent.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: When $5.0\text{ g}$ of magnesium reacts with $20.0\text{ g}$ of oxygen gas according to the reaction: $$2\text{Mg}(s) + \text{O}_2 (g) \right arrow 2\text{MgO}(s)$$ What is the mass of $\text{MgO}$ that can be formed?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Molar mass of $\text{Mg} = 24.3\text{ g/mol}$, $\text{O}_2 = 32.0\text{ g/mol}$, and $\text{MgO} = 40.3\text{ g/mol}$. Moles of $\text{Mg} = 5.0 / 24.3 = 0.2058\text{ mol}$; moles of $\text{O}_2 = 20.0 / 32.0 = 0.625\text{ mol}$. Magnesium is the limiting reactant. Yield: $$0.2058\text{ mol} \times 40.3\text{ g/mol} = 8.29\text{ g} \approx 8.3\text{ g}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A student crushes a large crystal of sugar into many small pieces before dissolving it in water. The sugar dissolves faster than the large crystal. Which of the following is correctly describing the observation?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Subdividing a large crystal into smaller particles increases the surface area exposed to the surrounding solvent molecules, accelerating the dissolution process.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A technician prepares a solution by dissolving $40\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$, in enough water to make $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. What is the molarity ($\text{M}$) of this solution?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Molar mass of $\text{NaOH} = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40.0\text{ g/mol}$. Moles of $\text{NaOH} = 40\text{ g} / 40\text{ g/mol} = 1.0\text{ mol}$. Volume = $500\text{ mL} = 0.500\text{ L}$. Molarity $$M = \frac{1.0\text{ mol}}{0.500\text{ L}} = 2.0\text{ M}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following oxides is classified as an amphoteric oxide?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) is an amphoteric oxide because it can react with both strong acids (forming aluminum salts) and strong bases (forming aluminate ions).

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
Which of the following statements correctly applies to the formation and nature of salts?
I. $\text{NaHSO}_4$ is a normal salt because all ionizable $\text{H}^+$ from the acid are replaced. II. $\text{NaHSO}_4$ is acidic salt formed when ionizable $\text{H}^+$ of the acid is not completely replaced by metal ions. III. $\text{Zn (OH) Cl}$ is a basic salt because it contains one ionizable $\text{OH}^-$ group in its formula. IV. $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a basic salt due to the presence of $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ that can be hydrolysis.
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Statement I is incorrect because $\text{NaHSO}_4$ has an unreplaced ionizable proton. Statements II (acid salt), III (basic salt with hydroxy group), and IV (salt of strong base + weak acid that undergoes anion hydrolysis to yield alkaline solution) are all correct.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: In a Galvanic cell consisting of Zinc and Copper elect rodes, which of the following process occurs at the anode electrode?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In a Daniell galvanic cell, the anode is the negative electrode where oxidation takes place: $\text{Zn}(s) \right arrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following statement is correctly describing the reaction represented in the diagram below?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In the potential energy diagram, the enthalpy of the products is lower than that of the reactants ($H_{\text{products}} < H_{\text{reactants}}$), so $\Delta H = H_p - H_r < 0$, signifying an exothermic reaction that releases heat.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: In the extraction of Iron using a blast furnace, what is the primary purpose of adding Limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$) to the furnace?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Limestone thermally decomposes into calcium oxide ($\text{CaO}$), which acts as a basic flux reacting with acidic sand/silica impurities ($\text{SiO}_2$) to form molten calcium silicate slag ($\text{CaSiO}_3$) that floats and is tapped off.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Non-metals usually have poor electrical conductivity and are often brittle. However, they are widely used in electrical insulation and chemical industries. Which evaluation best explain how these properties affect their real-world uses?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Because non-metals lack free mobile valence electrons, they are non-conductive and serve as vital electrical insulators, though their mechanical brittleness limits their utility in load-bearing structural tasks.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: What is the correct IUPAC name for this molecule?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain contains 10 carbons (decane). Numbering from the left gives substituents at positions 3, 4, and 5. Alphabetical ordering: bromo before diethyl before methyl yields 3,4-dibromo-5,5-diethyl-3-methyldecane.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Abel is a grade 10 student. He took three different test tubes and added $5.00\text{ mL}$ of toluene to each test tube. Then he added 2 drops of $\text{Br}_2$ water in the first test tube, equal drops of cold $\text{KMnO}_4$ in the second test tube and again equal drops of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the third test tube. In which test tube does a reaction occur?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Toluene is an aromatic hydrocarbon that does not react with aqueous bromine water without a Lewis acid catalyst/UV light, nor does it react with cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$ (oxidation of the methyl side chain requires heating). However, toluene undergoes electrophilic aromatic sulfonation with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at room temperature.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following is the major limit ation of the Arrhenius concept of acids and bases?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The Arrhenius theory restricts acids and bases strictly to substances that dissociate to produce $\text{H}^+$ or $\text{OH}^-$ ions in water (aqueous medium), failing to account for acid-base behaviors in gas phases or non-aqueous solvents.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A grade 12 student prepares $0.20\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of Acetic acid in the laboratory, according to the ionization equation given: $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+(aq) + \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-(aq): K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$$ Which of the following is the closest approximation of the hydrogen ion concentration? (Given $\sqrt{3.6} = 1.9$)
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: For a weak monoprotic acid: $$[\text{H}^+] = \sqrt{K_a \cdot C_a} = \sqrt{1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.20} = \sqrt{3.6 \times 10^{-6}} = 1.9 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Consider a solution that is $0.10\text{ M}$ acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and $0.20\text{ M}$ sodium acetate ($\text{NaCH}_3\text{COO}$). Which of the following statements is correct?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: This is an acidic buffer solution. Adding a small amount of strong acid ($\text{HCl}$) is buffered by acetate ions ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \right arrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$), resulting in only a slight decrease in $\text{pH}$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following procedure can NOT produce buffer solution?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Mixing $\text{NaOH}$ with excess strong acid $\text{HCl}$ produces $\text{NaCl}$ and residual $\text{HCl}$. Since both are strong electrolytes with no weak conjugate pair, it cannot function as a buffer.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A buffer solution is prepared using Acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and its conjugate base Sodium acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$). Under which condition will this buffer solution have maximum buffering capacity?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Maximum buffer capacity occurs when the concentrations of weak acid and conjugate base are equal ($[\text{HA}] = [\text{A}^-]$), at which point $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a$ according to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following salts will produce an acidic solution when dissolved in water?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) is the salt of a weak base ($\text{NH}_3$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$). The $\text{NH}_4^+$ cat i on hydrolyzes in water to produce hydronium ions: $\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: The dye bromothymol blue ($\text{HBb}$) is a weak acid whose ionization can be represented as follows: $$\text{HBb}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+(aq) + \text{Bb}^-(aq)$$ Which way will the equilibrium shift when $\text{NaOH}$ is added?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Adding $\text{NaOH}$ introduces hydroxide ions ($\text{OH}^-$), which react with $\text{H}^+$ to form water. By Le Chatelier's Principle, removing $\text{H}^+$ shifts the equilibrium to the right.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: During laboratory class, a student placed clean water in a beaker and added pieces of calcium metal using tongs. Which of the following is observed color after the reaction has completed?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Calcium reacts with water to form basic calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas: $\text{Ca}(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \right arrow \text{Ca (OH)}_2 (aq) + \text{H}_2 (g)$. The resulting alkaline solution turns red litmus paper blue.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following statement is NOT correctly describe about oxidation and reduction?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: By definition (OIL RIG): Oxidation is the Loss of electrons, and Reduction is the Gain of electrons. Statement C incorrectly reverses this definition.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A chemist compares electrolysis of dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution and concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ solution using inert elect rodes. The substance produced at anode electrode of dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution and concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ solution are _____ and _____ respectively.
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution, water oxidation dominates at the anode producing Oxygen ($\text{O}_2$). In concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ (brine), chloride ion discharge is favored due to high concentration and chlorine over potential, producing Chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$).

exam-model-1789960911494.text: An aqueous solution contains $\text{Ag}^+(aq)$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$ ions. Electrolysis is carried out using inert platinum elect rodes. A constant current of $9.65\text{ A}$ is passed through the solution for $1000\text{ seconds}$. Which metal will be deposited at the cathode and what mass will be deposited?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Because $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V} > E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}$, silver ions reduce first at the cathode. Charge $Q = I \times t = 9.65\text{ A} \times 1000\text{ s} = 9650\text{ C} = 0.10\text{ mol } e^-$. Moles of $\text{Ag} = 0.10\text{ mol}$. Mass $= 0.10\text{ mol} \times 108\text{ g/mol} = 10.8\text{ g}$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A Galvanic cell constructed from a strip of magnesium metal dipped in a solution of magnesium sulfate and a strip of silver metal immersed in a solution of silver nitrate. Which of the following correctly represents the cell not ation for this galvanic cell?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: By convention, the anode (oxidation of $\text{Mg}$) is written on the left, followed by the double vertical line for the salt bridge, and the cathode (reduction of $\text{Ag}^+$) on the right: $\text{Mg} | \text{Mg}^{2+} || \text{Ag}^+ | \text{Ag}$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Aluminum metal reacts spontaneously with iron (II) ions according to the reaction: $$2\text{Al}(s) + 3\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) \right arrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(aq) + 3\text{Fe}(s)$$ What is the value of $\Delta G^\circ$ for the reaction?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = -0.44\text{ V} - (-1.66\text{ V}) = +1.22\text{ V}$. For $n = 6\text{ mol } e^-$: $$\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ = -6 \times 96500\text{ C/mol} \times 1.22\text{ V} = -706380\text{ J} = -706.4\text{ kJ} \approx -706\text{ kJ}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: A metal pipe line buried under ground is protected from corrosion by attaching a more reactive metal such as magnesium. Why does magnesium protect the iron pipe?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Magnesium has a more negative standard reduction potential than iron, preferentially undergoing oxidation as a sacrificial anode to supply electrons and protect the iron cathode from corroding.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following is considered a renewable resource?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Solar energy is inexhaustible and naturally replenished on a human time scale, making it a renewable resource unlike fossil fuels.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: At which stage of industrial manufacturing process of sulphuric acid, vanadium (V) oxide specifically required to ensure efficient industrial production?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In the Contact Process, vanadium (V) oxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$) is used as the heterogeneous catalyst during the exothermic catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide: $2\text{SO}_2 (g) + \text{O}_2 (g) \xrightarrow{\text{V}_2\text{O}_5} 2\text{SO}_3 (g)$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which one of the following fertilizers supplies the highest percentage of nitrogen to plants?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Urea ($\text{CO (NH}_2)_2$) has a molar mass of $60.06\text{ g/mol}$ and contains 2 nitrogen atoms ($28.02\text{ g}$), delivering a nitrogen content of $\approx 46.7\%$, the highest of all solid nitrogenous fertilizers.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following describes the process of manufacturing valuable products in industries?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Chemical industrial manufacturing entails systematic engineering processes that convert raw chemical feedstocks into valuable commercial commodities utilizing control led energy inputs.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which type of glass is made by heating a mixture of silica, sodium carbonate and limestone?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Soda-lime glass is the most common commercial glass, produced by fusing silica sand ($\text{SiO}_2$), soda ash ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$), and limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$).

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following chemicals is commonly known as washing soda?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Washing soda is the common name for hydrated sodium carbonate decahydrate ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$). $\text{NaHCO}_3$ is baking soda, and $\text{NaOH}$ is caustic soda.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following chemicals is mainly used to kill unwanted plants in agricultural fields?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Herbicides are agrochemical formulations specifically designed to control, suppress, or eradicate unwanted vegetation and weeds.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following is NOT the Methods of reducing water pollution.
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Applying excessive agricultural chemicals and fertilizers causes extensive nutrient run off and eutrophication in fresh water ecosystems.

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
Consider the following steps involved in the preparation of local alcohol (Araki):
I: Fermentation of the mixture which converts sugars into ethanol. II: Preparation of the raw materials by crushing cereals and mixing them with water. III: Distill ation of the fermented mixture to separate ethanol from water. IV: Heating the fermented mixture to produce alcohol vapor, later condenses to liquid alcohol. Which of the following shows the correct sequence of steps in the preparation of local alcohol (Araki)?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The traditional process begins with grain crushing and mash preparation (II), followed by yeast fermentation into alcohol (I), thermal heating/evaporating (IV), and finally condensation/distillation collection (III).

exam-model-1789960911494.text: What is the molar mass of a polyethylene sample, $[-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-]_n$, when $n = 4600$?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: The molar mass of the repeat unit $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-$ is $2 (12.01) + 4 (1.008) = 28.05\text{ g/mol}$. Total molar mass: $$M = 4600 \times 28.0\text{ g/mol} = 128,800\text{ g/mol} = 1.288 \times 10^5\text{ g/mol}$$

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which one of the following polymer-monomer pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is synthesized from tetrafluoroethene ($F_2C=CF_2$), not propylene. Polypropylene is made from propene.

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
A student compared thermoplastic polymers and thermosetting polymers.

$$

| | \text{Thermoplastic polymers} | \text{Thermosetting polymers} |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| \text{A} | \text{soften and reshaped when heated} | \text{permanently hard after heating} |
| \text{B} | \text{consist mainly of linear chains} | \text{highly cross-linked three-dimensional structures} |
| \text{C} | \text{Can't repeatedly melted and remolded} | \text{soften when heated and can be reshaped again} |
| \text{D} | \text{are generally recyclable} | \text{Can't be recyclable} |

$$

Which of the following pairs is NOT correct about their difference?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Pair C is completely inverted. Thermoplastics can be repeatedly melted, remolded, and reshaped upon heating, whereas thermosets decompose and cannot be softened once cured.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: For the electrolysis of aqueous copper (II) sulfate solution using graphite electrode, what substances produced at anode and cathode electrode respectively and their ratio?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: At the anode, water oxidizes: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \right arrow \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^-$ ($1\text{ mol } \text{O}_2 / 4e^-$). At the cathode, copper reduces: $2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4e^- \right arrow 2\text{Cu}$ ($2\text{ mol } \text{Cu} / 4e^-$). Hence, $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Cu}$ are generated in a $1:2$ molar ratio.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which one of the following reactions creates energy in our bodies during respiration?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Aerobic cellular respiration combusts glucose with oxygen to yield carbon dioxide, water, and ATP energy: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + 6\text{O}_2 \right arrow 6\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Energy}$.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: The following gases are contributed to the green house effect on Earth. Which is the correct order of their importance from greatest to smallest in the natural green house effect?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: In Earth's atmosphere, water vapor ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) contributes roughly $36-70\%$ of the green house effect, followed by carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$, $9-26\%$) and methane ($\text{CH}_4$, $4-9\%$).

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following sample routine correctly indicate the extraction of copper from is principal-ore?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Metallurgical extraction of copper proceeds sequentially: 1) Froth flotation concentration, 2) Roasting sulfide ore in air, 3) Smelting reduction to blister copper, 4) Electrolytic refining purification.

exam-model-1789960911494.text: Which of the following is TRUE about a homologous series?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: A homologous series is a series of organic compounds possessing the same general formula and functional group, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a methylene ($-\text{CH}_2-$) unit.

exam-model-1789960911494.text:
The following reaction can be used for the synthesis of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$ as a desired product:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{S}^- \long right arrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{SH} + \text{Br}^-$$
What is the atom economy for the above reaction?
exam-model-1789960911494.explanation: Atom economy is given by: $$\text{Atom Economy} = \frac{\text{Molar mass of desired product}}{\text{Total molar mass of all reactants}} \times 100\%$$ Desired product $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8 = 4 (12.0) + 8 (1.0) = 56.0\text{ g/mol}$. Reactants: $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br} (136.9) + \text{CH}_3\text{S}^- (47.1) = 184.0\text{ g/mol}$. $$\text{Atom Economy} = \frac{56.0}{184.0} \times 100\% = 30.43\% \approx 30.4\%$$

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which one of the following words is composed of some letters appearing in an alphabetical order?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The word " hijack " contains the letters " h ", " i ", and " j " in consecutive alphabetical sequence (h -> i -> j).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Statement: Currently, many workers in the company have become punctual. Assumption I: All the workers must have bought their own automobiles. Assumption II: Previously, many of the workers were late to work. Assumption III: Employers are now more serious about lateness to work. Assumption IV: The productivity of the company has become questionable. Which one of the assumptions is logically related with the above statement?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: When workers suddenly " become punctual," it inherently presumes they were frequently tardy before (Assumption II). In organizational behavior, such widespread behavioral corrections typically stem from management taking strict administrative measures against tardiness (Assumption III). Therefore, Assumptions II and III are directly and logically related.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Ms. Y is Ms. X ' s mother, and Mr. P is Ms. Y ' s only brother. Mr. Z is Mr. P ' s son. Thus, how is Mr. Z related to Ms. X?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Ms. Y is Ms. X ' s mother. Mr. P is Ms. Y ' s brother, which makes Mr. P the maternal uncle of Ms. X. Mr. Z is the son of Mr. P (the uncle's child). Therefore, Mr. Z and Ms. X are first cousins (maternal cousins).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Statement: Many universities are replacing printed resources with on line resources. Therefore, students can have better access for resources to learn effectively. Based on the above statement, which one of the following options is valid?
options: Universities are giving priority to save money.
Printed resources are better than digital resources.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The prompt explicitly states that replacing printed materials with on line resources allows students to " have better access for resources to learn effectively," directly establishing that on line resources enhance students' learning.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which one of the following words has three letters in sequence in any of its parts when read inverted?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Reversing (inverting) the word " federal " gives " laredef ". Within " laredef ", the substring " def " consists of three consecutive alphabetical letters (d -> e -> f).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Statement: Sheep, animals and furry animals exist. All sheep are furry animals. All animals are not sheep. Conclusion I: Some animals are furry animals. Conclusion II: All furry animals are sheep. Conclusion III: No animals are furry animals. Conclusion IV: No furry animals are animals. Which of the above conclusions can be logically drawn from the preceding statement?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: All sheep are animals and all sheep are furry animals. Because the set of sheep is non-empty and constitutes a subset of animals that are furry, it logically follows that " Some animals are furry animals " (Conclusion I).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: If the word " INTRODUCE " is rewritten maintaining the natural order of the letters in it. Which letter appears 7th from the left end?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
Arranging the letters of " INTRODUCE " in standard alphabetical order gives:
1: C, 2: D, 3: E, 4: I, 5: N, 6: O, 7: R, 8: T, 9: U. The 7th letter from the left end is R.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Statement I: Yesterday a heavy truck over turned on a high way. Statement II: Police cord oned off the whole locality for half a day. Which one of the following is true about the relationship between the two statements?
options: Statement I is the cause; statement II is its effect.
Both statements are caused by independent reasons.
Statement II is the cause; statement I is the effect.
There is no relationship between the two statements.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The over turning of a heavy truck on a high way created an immediate emergency and hazardous situation (Statement I = Cause), which directly led to the police cord oning off the area for security and investigation (Statement II = Effect).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: While Ms. X is a sociable girl, her younger sister is a bit <u>**DOUR**</u>. Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bold word 'dour'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Dour " means sullen, gloomy, stern, or unfriendly. In contrast to " sociable ", its most direct antonym among the options is " friendly ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The man looks ancient; he must be above fifty. Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bold word 'ancient'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Here, " ancient " is used hyperbolically to refer to an elderly person. The direct opposite of old/aged in reference to an individual's physical age is " young ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The woman be came <u>**INDIGNANT**</u> at the unfair way she had been treated. Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bold word 'indignant'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Indignant " describes feeling righteous anger or resentment at perceived injustice. Among the given options, " excited " (conveying positive, enthusiastic feeling) represents the best antonymic valence.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Having taken too much alcohol, the man be came so <u>**INTOXICATED**</u> that he could not stand alone. Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the bold word 'intoxicated'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Intoxicated " means heavily affected by alcohol (inebriated/drunk). The exact antonym for someone not under the influence of alcohol is " sober ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
Read Passage I:
" The growing influence of social media has created significant responsibilities for both platform designers and users. Managing this influence responsibly requires a balanced approach that protects societal well-being while preserving the advantages of digital connectivity. Central to this responsibility are digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical engagement. Users must be equipped with the skills to evaluate information sources, recognize persuasive techniques, and engage thoughtfully with on line content..."

What are the driving human traits for managing the social media in an effective manner?
options: digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical engagement
intelligence, immersive media, and augmented reality
cultural identities, public opinion, and social movements
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The passage explicitly states: " Central to this responsibility are digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical engagement."

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which line does provide the evidence for the answer to question number 13?
options: Lines 12 - 14 [When users ... actively rather than passively.]
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Lines 4-5 contain the exact textual citation: " Central to this responsibility are digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical engagement."

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Where does the sphere of social media's influence mainly rest on?
options: artificial intelligence, immersive media, and augmented reality
technological innovation and stakeholder's critical engagement
transparency in algorithmic design and content moderation
formal education and informal learning opportunities
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The conclusion of the passage notes that the ultimate impact of social media rests on " both technological innovation and the collective choices made by all stakeholders " (stakeholders' critical engagement).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Where does the writer pin point the supporting evidence to your answer to question number 15?
options: Lines 5 - 7 [Users must be...engage thoughtfully with online content.]
Lines 17 - 19 [As this influence expands ... increasingly important.]
Lines 19 - 21 [The future impact...choices made by all stakeholders.]
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Lines 19-21 formulate the closing thes is: " The future impact of social media will depend on both technological innovation and the collective choices made by all stakeholders."

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The Club finally managed to get a/an __________ trophy thanks to its determined players' pers is tent performance.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Hard-earned " is the most natural and semantically appropriate collocation used to describe an achievement or trophy secured through pers is tent dedication and strenuous effort.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: It is evident in history that it took a lot for the Italians to fully recover from the __________ of their defeat at the Battle of Adwa.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The catastrophic defeat suffered by the invading colonial Italian army at the Battle of Adwa in 1896 produced profound geopolitical and psychological " humiliation " for Italy.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Following the Corridor Development in the city, some drivers are being __________ with money for driving their cars on pavements dedicated to pedestrians.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: When traffic violators are required to pay money as a penalty for illegal driving, they are " fined ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The king having been __________ from his throne by the military, he fled to a neighboring state.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: In political context, a monarch relinquishing or being forced off the royal throne is said to have " abdicated " (or forced abdication). Because he was alive to flee to a neighboring state, " assassin ated " is ruled out.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The jury was nominated last Friday at the Federal First Instant Court to pass its final __________ on the request of the suspect to be released on bail.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: A court of law or judicial panel passes a formal " decision " (ruling/verdict) on bail applications and petitions.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The United Nations Security Council passed a/an __________ decision, without any difference on Israel that it leaves Gaza for the Pales tin i ans.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: A resolution passed " without any difference " (total agreement among all voting delegates) is defined as a " unanimous " decision.

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
Read Passage II:
" People often believe that successful individuals share three main qualities: motivation, ability, and opportunity. According to this view, success comes from hard work, natural talent, and a bit of luck. However, these factors alone do not fully explain why some people succeed more than others. An important factor that is often over looked is how people interact with others. In everyday work situations, individuals must decide whether to focus only on their own benefit or to help others without expecting immediate rewards..."

Which one of the following is mostly over looked in dealing with success?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The passage notes: " An important factor that is often over looked is how people interact with others," which refers directly to the role of interpersonal transactions and reciprocal behaviors.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which of the following could be the most appropriate title to this passage?
options: How do personal effort and success interrelate?
Who is benefitted from the success?
success and the role of interpersonal behavior
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The core thes is of the entire excerpt investigates how giving, taking, and interpersonal relationships determine long-term work place achievement, making " success and the role of interpersonal behavior " the most fitting title.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: According to the writer, which of the following ideas are the two major points of views regarding the contributing factors for one's success?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The passage establishes that success is shaped both by traditional individual factors (hard work, ability, personal effort) and social dynamics (how people treat others, interact, and communicate).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: In paragraph 2, what does the phrase " these differences " denote?
options: some expect more than they deserve, and in return give scanty
the differences between the findings of psychology and others
if people are ready to help others, or give priority to themselves
believing in industriousness versus being harmonious to others
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " These differences " directly follows the statement about differing attitudes toward giving and receiving help—specifically contrasting takers (putting themselves first) with givers (ready to support others).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: COMPASS : DIRECTION; Altimeter : __________
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: A compass is an instrument specifically designed to measure or indicate direction; an altimeter is an instrument used to measure altitude (height above sea level).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: GUM : STICK; Needle : __________
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Stick " is the standard countable unit or primary physical form of gum (a stick of gum); a " stitch " is the fundamental unit of work/action created by a needle.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: RIGHT : WRONG; Left : __________
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The word " RIGHT " is paired with its moral/logical antonym " WRONG ". Therefore, " Left " must be paired with its directional antonym " Right ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text: WING : LIFT; Motor : __________
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: A wing generates aerodynamic lift to keep an aircraft airborne; a motor/engine generates mechanical thrust to propel the vehicle forward.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: EROSION : SOIL; Corrosion : __________
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Erosion is the physical wearing away and degradation of soil; corrosion is the chemical degradation and oxidation of metal.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Working <u>**UNDERCOVER**</u>, the journalist discovered the illegal payments. Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to the bold word 'under cover'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Under cover " refers to engaging in an investigation covertly and in secret without revealing one's true identity.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The association pledged a 10-million-birr support for our plan. Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to the bold word 'pledged'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: To " pledge " financial assistance means to make a solemn formal promise or commitment to deliver the specified funds.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The manager settled the problem by taking a <u>**SAGACIOUS**</u> decision that could satisfy the parties with a polarized stance. Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to the bold word 'sagacious'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: " Sagacious " means having or showing keen mental discernment, good judgment, and insightful practical wisdom (wise).

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The abduction of the president by a foreign nation was condemned by many countries on the ground that it was against the principles of international law. Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to the bold word 'condemned'.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: To " condemn " an unlawful action means to formally express strong public disapproval of it, which is synonymous with " denounced ".

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Consider the parallelogram ABCD. If DC = 10 cm, M and N are midpoints of DC and AB respectively, and the area of triangle ADM is 20 cm², then what is the area of parallelogram ANCM in cm²?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Since M is the midpoint of DC (length 10 cm), DM = MC = 5 cm. Similarly, AN = NB = 5 cm. The area of triangle ADM = 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * 5 * h = 20 cm². Solving for height h: 2.5 * h = 20 ⇒ h = 8 cm. Parallelogram ANCM has base MC = 5 cm and the same perpendicular height h = 8 cm. Area (ANCM) = base * height = 5 * 8 = 40 cm².

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
Let x - y = 2, and x² + y² = 10, where x, y ∈ ℝ and x > 0, y > 0. Quantity A: x⁴ + y⁴ - 9/(xy) Quantity B: 79
Which one of the following is true?
options: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
1) Squaring (x - y): (x - y)² = x² - 2xy + y² ⇒ 2² = (x² + y²) - 2xy ⇒ 4 = 10 - 2xy ⇒ 2xy = 6 ⇒ xy = 3.
2) Squaring (x² + y²): (x² + y²)² = x⁴ + 2 (xy)² + y⁴ ⇒ 10² = (x⁴ + y⁴) + 2 (3²) ⇒ 100 = (x⁴ + y⁴) + 18 ⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 82.
3) Evaluating Quantity A: (x⁴ + y⁴) - 9/(xy) = 82 - 9/3 = 82 - 3 = 79. Since Quantity A = 79 and Quantity B = 79, Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: If l₁: y = m₁x + b₁ and l₂: y = m₂x + b₂ are two lines with m₁ ≠ 0 and m₂ ≠ 0, then which one of the following is NOT true?
options: If m₁m₂ = -1, then the two lines are perpendicular.
If m₁ = m₂, then the two lines have no common point.
If m₁ = m₂, then the two lines are parallel.
If m₁ ≠ m₂, then the two lines are intersecting lines.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: If m₁ = m₂ and also b₁ = b₂, the two lines are coincident (identical), meaning they share infinitely many common points. Thus, stating they have " no common point " is NOT uncondition ally true.

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
Let △DCE be a right-angled triangle with right angle at D that inscribes a circle with center O and radius r = 5 m. The side DC is 12 m long and all sides are tangent to the circle. Quantity A: The length of side CE (hypotenuse) Quantity B: 36 meters
Which one of the following is true?
options: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
For a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, the inradius formula is r = (a + b - c)/2. Here, leg a = DC = 12 m, r = 5 m, leg b = DE, and hypotenuse c = √(12² + b²).
5 = (12 + b - √(144 + b²))/2 ⇒ 10 = 12 + b - √(144 + b²) ⇒ √(144 + b²) = b + 2. Squaring both sides: 144 + b² = b² + 4b + 4 ⇒ 140 = 4b ⇒ b = 35 m. Hypotenuse CE = c = √(12² + 35²) = √(144 + 1225) = √1369 = 37 m. Since Quantity A (CE = 37 m) is greater than Quantity B (36 m), Quantity A is greater.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: The number of bacteria in a certain colony was 5000 initially. If the rate at which the number of bacteria grows is 10% per day, then what will be the number of bacteria at the end of the second day?
The price of one kilogram coffee was Birr 800 last year. This year the price becomes Birr 1040. What is the percentage increase of the price of coffee?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Price increase = 1040 - 800 = 240 Birr. Percentage Increase = (240 / 800) * 100% = 30%.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which one of the following units is used in measuring area?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Area is measured in squared units of length, such as millimeter square (mm²). Centimeter and meter are linear units, while meter cube is a volume unit.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: Which one of the following is the simplified form of (x - 2 + 1/x) / (x - 1/x) for x ≠ 0, 1, -1?
Which one of the following is the simplified form of √200 + 3√8?
If the sum of a number and its reciprocal is equal to 82 times its reciprocal, then which one of the following is a possible number?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Let the number be x: x + 1/x = 82/x. Multiplying both sides by x: x² + 1 = 82 ⇒ x² = 81 ⇒ x = ±9. From the given options, 9 is the correct solution.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: A transport company charges Birr 70 plus Birr 15 per kilometer. At the end of your travel if you pay Birr 250, then how long did you travel in kms?
If a car moves at a constant speed of 75 kilometer per hour, then how long does it take to cover a distance of 325 kilometer?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Time = Distance / Speed = 325 / 75 = 13 / 3 hours = 4 1/3 hours = 4 hours and (1/3 * 60) minutes = 4 hours and 20 minutes.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: A person has a fencing material of length 100m. He wants to enclose a rectangular region for his dogs and also needs to have a 2m gate at one corner. What is the maximum area he can enclose in m²?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
The total perimeter of the rectangular fence minus the 2 m un-fenced gate is 100 m:
2x + 2y - 2 = 100 ⇒ 2 (x + y) = 102 ⇒ x + y = 51. To maximize area A = x * y with x + y = 51, we choose a square where x = y = 51/2 = 25.5 m. Maximum Area = (51/2)² = 2601 / 4 m² = 650.25 m².

exam-2018-social-sat.text: If x : y : z = 2 : 3 : 5 and y = 60, then what is the value of x + z?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Let the common scaling factor be k: y = 3k = 60 ⇒ k = 20. Then x = 2k = 2 * 20 = 40, and z = 5k = 5 * 20 = 100. Sum x + z = 40 + 100 = 140.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: If the roots of the quadratic equation x² - mx + k = 0 are two consecutive integers, then what is the value of m² - 4k?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
Let the consecutive roots be n and n + 1. By Vieta's formulas: Sum of roots m = n + (n + 1) = 2n + 1. Product of roots k = n (n + 1) = n² + n. Now calculate m² - 4k:
(2n + 1)² - 4 (n² + n) = (4n² + 4n + 1) - (4n² + 4n) = 1.

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
Based on the profit table:
Combined profits for shops P, Q, R, S is Birr 500,000 in 2022 with a profit ratio of 4:5:6:5 in 2022. In 2023: P (+15%), Q (+30%), R (+15%), S (+10%). What is the difference (in Birr) between the total profit of shop R in 2023 and the total profit of shop S in 2023?
What is the percentage increase on shop Q from 2022 to 2025? (Given: 2023: +30%, 2024: -25%, 2025: +20%)
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Multiplier for shop Q from 2022 to 2025 = 1.30 * 0.75 * 1.20 = 1.17. Percentage increase = (1.17 - 1) * 100% = 17%.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: What percentage (approximately) of all shops' combined profit in 2022 increased in 2025?
What is the ratio between the total profit from shop S in 2023 to the total profit from shop S in 2024?
How much less (in Birr) did all profit make in 2024 compared to all profit in 2023?
Which one of the following is the simplified form of (a³b^(1/2))⁴ / (a⁶b³)?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Numerator: (a³b^(1/2))⁴ = (a³)^4 * (b^(1/2))^4 = a¹² * b². Expression = (a¹²b²) / (a⁶b³) = a^(12 - 6) * b^(2 - 3) = a⁶ * b^(-1) = a⁶/b.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: In a bag there are eight cards numbered from 1 to 8. If we draw one card at random, then what is the probability of getting a prime number?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: Sample space S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} (total 8 cards). Prime numbers in S = {2, 3, 5, 7} (4 primes). Probability = 4 / 8 = 1/2.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: If two six faces dice are thrown together, then what is the probability that the two numbers on the upper faces are NOT relatively prime?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation:
Total outcomes = 6 * 6 = 36. Pairs with gcd (a, b) > 1 (not coprime):
- Even pairs (gcd ≥ 2): (2,2), (2,4), (2,6), (4,2), (4,4), (4,6), (6,2), (6,4), (6,6) → 9 pairs
- Divisible by 3 (not both even): (3,3), (3,6), (6,3) → 3 pairs
- Divisible by 5: (5,5) → 1 pair
Total pairs that are NOT relatively prime = 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 pairs. Probability = 13/36.

exam-2018-social-sat.text:
In the number pyramid shown:
Row 1 (base): [4, 2, 3, 7]
Row 2: [5, 4, 9]
Row 3: [8, 12]
Row 4 (top): [x] 
Which one of the following numbers is the value of x?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The pyramid generates each upper brick from the two adjacent lower bricks by the rule: Upper = Left + Right - 1. Row 2: 4 + 2 - 1 = 5; 2 + 3 - 1 = 4; 3 + 7 - 1 = 9. Row 3: 5 + 4 - 1 = 8; 4 + 9 - 1 = 12. Row 4 (top): x = 8 + 12 - 1 = 19.

exam-2018-social-sat.text: By using a certain formula using a digit number 12345 we obtained 29 and using some pattern from the digit number 23456 we obtained 126 then which one of the following numbers is obtained from the digit number 3456?
exam-2018-social-sat.explanation: The arithmetic pattern is: multiply all digits except the last one, then add the last digit. For 12345: (1 * 2 * 3 * 4) + 5 = 24 + 5 = 29. For 23456: (2 * 3 * 4 * 5) + 6 = 120 + 6 = 126. For 3456: (3 * 4 * 5) + 6 = 60 + 6 = 66.

exam-2018-social-math.text: If a = -2√3 + 3√2 - 2 and b = -3√2 + 2, then a + b is equal to:
If b is a fixed positive number, which one of the following is true about graphs of the given linear functions?
options: The graph of f(x) = -2x - b is straight line.
The graph of f(x) = bx is horizontal.
The graph of f(x) = -2x + b is increasing.
The graph of f(x) = 2x - b is decreasing.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Any first-degree polynomial function of the form f (x) = mx + c represents a straight line on the Cartes i an plane. Since f (x) = -2x - b has slope m = -2 and y-intercept -b, its graph is a straight line.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Consider a circle that has diameter AB of length 8 cm. If you fold the circle over AB, then what is the area of the part of the circle on one part of the diameter (in cm²)?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Given diameter d = 8 cm, the radius r = 4 cm. Total area of the circle = πr² = π(4)² = 16π cm². Folding the circle across its diameter AB divides the circle into two identical semicircles. The area of one semicircular part = (16π) / 2 = 8π cm².

exam-2018-social-math.text:
Let A = 
[ 3 -3 6 ]
[ -6 9 12 ]
[ 12 -6 3 ]
Then 1/3 A is equal to:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Scalar multiplication of a matrix multiplies every single element in the matrix by 1/3:
Row 1: [3/3, -3/3, 6/3] = [1, -1, 2]
Row 2: [-6/3, 9/3, 12/3] = [-2, 3, 4]
Row 3: [12/3, -6/3, 3/3] = [4, -2, 1].

exam-2018-social-math.text: In how many different ways can 6 people be seated at a round table?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: The number of circular permutations of n distinct objects is given by (n - 1)!. For n = 6: (6 - 1)! = 5! = 5 * 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 120 ways.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
A library has registered the following data about daily book borrowers for ten consecutive days:
72, 84, 36, 84, 36, 30, 54, 92, 55, 83
What is the range of the data?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Range = Maximum Value - Minimum Value. Maximum value = 92, Minimum value = 30. Range = 92 - 30 = 62.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
The table shows the score of 12 students in mathematics:
Scores (x): 9, 7, 6, 5
Students (f): 4, 2, 4, 2
What is the mean score of the students?
Which one of the following is the value of sin(-600°)?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Adding 2 * 360° = 720° to find the positive coterminal angle:
-600° + 720° = 120°.
sin(-600°) = sin (120°) = sin (180° - 60°) = sin (60°) = √3/2.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the solution set of the greatest integer equation [1 - x] = 3?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
By definition of the floor (greatest integer) function, [u] = 3 ⇔ 3 ≤ u < 4.
3 ≤ 1 - x < 4
Subtract 1: 2 ≤ -x < 3
Multiply by -1 (reverses inequality signs): -2 ≥ x > -3 ⇔ -3 < x ≤ -2. In interval not ation, the solution set is (-3, -2].

exam-2018-social-math.text: When the circle (x - 3)² + (y - 1)² = 1 is reflected on a line y = 2x, then the image of the circle is:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Original circle center is C (3, 1) and radius r = 1. Reflecting the center point (3, 1) across the line y = 2x yields the reflected center C'(-1, 3). The radius remains r = 1 under reflect i on (i some try). Therefore, the image circle equation is (x - (-1))² + (y - 3)² = 1 ⇒ (x + 1)² + (y - 3)² = 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Let f (x) = x³ + 3x² - 9x + 7. Then, the graph of f is decreasing on:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
A function is decreasing where its first derivative f'(x) ≤ 0.
f'(x) = 3x² + 6x - 9 = 3 (x² + 2x - 3) = 3 (x + 3)(x - 1). Setting 3 (x + 3)(x - 1) ≤ 0 yields the closed interval [-3, 1].

exam-2018-social-math.text: A person deposits Birr 6000 at the end of each year into a saving account that pays 10% interest compounded annually. What is the future value of the annuity after 3 years?
What is the value of x in the equation 3 * ⁵√(3x)⁵ = 18?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Since ⁵√(3x)⁵ = 3x for odd roots:
3 * (3x) = 18 ⇒ 9x = 18 ⇒ x = 2.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What are the vertex and line of symmetry of the function y = 2x² - 4x + 3 respectively?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
For a quadratic y = ax² + bx + c:
x-coordinate of vertex = -b / (2a) = -(-4) / (2 * 2) = 4 / 4 = 1.
y-coordinate = 2 (1)² - 4 (1) + 3 = 2 - 4 + 3 = 1. Vertex is (1, 1) and the vertical axis of symmetry is x = 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Consider the circle centered at O, and a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD in the circle where angle A = (x + 40)°, angle B = 2x°, angle C = (2x - 10)°, and angle D = y°. What is the value of y?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite interior angles are supplementary (sum to 180°):
1) ∠A + ∠C = 180° ⇒ (x + 40) + (2x - 10) = 180° ⇒ 3x + 30 = 180° ⇒ 3x = 150° ⇒ x = 50°.
2) ∠B + ∠D = 180° ⇒ 2x + y = 180° ⇒ 2 (50°) + y = 180° ⇒ 100° + y = 180° ⇒ y = 80°.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
Which of the following matrices is row equivalent to matrix:
[ 2 -2 3 ]
 [ 2 1 0 ] 
[ 1 -1 -4 ]
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Performing elementary row operations:
Original: R1 = [2, -2, 3], R2 = [2, 1, 0], R3 = [1, -1, -4]. R2' = R1 - R2 = [2-2, -2-1, 3-0] = [0, -3, 3].
2*R3 - R1 = [2-2, -2-(-2), -8-3] = [0, 0, -11], which scaled is row equivalent to [0, 0, 11]. Thus, matrix B is row equivalent.

exam-2018-social-math.text: An outcome of a random experiment is said to be a favorable outcome if:
options: it can be predicted in advance.
it is the set of all possible results of the experiment.
it insures the occurrence of particular result.
it has equal chance of being chosen.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: In probability theory, a favorable outcome is any specific elementary event that satisfies the given condition of interest, there by insuring the occurrence of that particular specified event result.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Let L and S be the largest and smallest values of the given data respectively. The coefficient of range of the data is a relative measure given by:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: The coefficient of range is a dimensionless relative measure of dispersion defined as: Coefficient of Range = (L - S) / (L + S).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is true about a given natural number?
options: It is composite if it has more than two factors.
It is prime if it has exactly three factors.
It is composite if it has exactly two factors.
It is prime if it has more than two factors.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: A natural number greater than 1 is prime if it has exactly two positive distinct factors (1 and itself). A natural number is composite if it has strictly more than two positive factors.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is the use of standard deviation?
options: It gives the maximum value of the data.
It gives the average value of a given data.
It measures the scatter of a given data.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Standard deviation is a fundamental statistical metric that quantifies the amount of variation, dispersion, or scatter of a set of data values around their arithmetic mean.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is correct about trigonometric values of angles?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Since 157° and 23° are supplementary angles (157° + 23° = 180°):
sin (180° - θ) = sin(θ) ⇒ sin (157°) = sin (180° - 23°) = sin (23°).

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the simplified form of the expression ((x + 3)/x ÷ (x - 2)/(x - 3)) * ((x² - 2x)/(x² - 9)) over its domain?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Step 1: Invert and multiply the division part:
((x + 3)/x) * ((x - 3)/(x - 2)) = [(x + 3)(x - 3)] / [x (x - 2)] = (x² - 9) / [x (x - 2)]. Step 2: Multiply by the second term:
[(x² - 9) / (x (x - 2))] * [x (x - 2) / (x² - 9)] = 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
In a certain entrance examination, the following data of results is recorded:
12, 19, 15, 22, 53, 61, 57, 22, 18, 68, 72, 80, 83, 75, 76, 85, 85
Then, which one of the following is true about the data?
options: The value of Q3 - Q1 is 55.
The third quartile, Q3 of the data is 76.
The second quartile, Q2 of the data is 61.
The first quartile, Q1 of the data is 21.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Arranging all 17 observations in ascending order:
12, 15, 18, 19, 22, 22, 53, 57, [61] , 68, 72, 75, 76, 80, 83, 85, 85. Since n = 17, the med i an (second quartile Q2) is the 9th observation = 61.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Water is being poured into a circular cylinder of radius 50 cm at a rate of change of volume 5000π cm³/sec. What is the rate of change of height of the level of water in the cylinder when the height is 40 cm?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Volume of a cylinder: V = πr²h. Since radius r = 50 cm is constant:
V = π(50)²h = 2500π h. Different i ating with respect to time t:
dV/dt = 2500π (dh/dt).
5000π = 2500π (dh/dt) ⇒ dh/dt = 5000π / 2500π = 2 cm/sec.

exam-2018-social-math.text: For a ≥ 0, which one of the following numbers is NOT equal to a^(2/5)?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: (a⁵)^(1/2) = a^(5 * 1/2) = a^(5/2), which is NOT equal to a^(2/5). All other options simplify exactly to a^(2/5).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the diagrams represents a vector with direction East 42° South?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: A direction of East 42° South starts pointing toward East (positive x-axis) and rotates 42° clock wise toward South (negative y-axis) into the 4th quadrant, which is correctly illustrated in Diagram D.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Let x be an angle in the second quadrant. If tan x = -√3, then which of the following is true about the other trigonometric values of angle x?
Which one of the following is true about the function f defined by f (x) = (3x² + 3x - 6) / (x² - 1)?
options: Its x-intercepts are (-2, 0) and (1, 0), and its y-intercept is (0, 6).
Its x-intercepts are (-2, 0) and (1, 0), and its y-intercept is (0, -6).
Its x-intercept is (1, 0) and its y-intercept is (0, -6).
Its x-intercept is (-2, 0) and its y-intercept is (0, 6).
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
f (x) = [3 (x + 2)(x - 1)] / [(x - 1)(x + 1)] = 3 (x + 2) / (x + 1) for x ≠ 1. Setting f (x) = 0 ⇒ x = -2 (x = 1 is a removable discontinuity / hole, not an intercept).
y-intercept: f (0) = 3 (0 + 2)/(0 + 1) = 6 ⇒ (0, 6). Therefore, x-intercept is (-2, 0) and y-intercept is (0, 6).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is NOT true about the mode of the given data?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: When all data values are identical (12, 12, 12, 12, 12), the mode is 12 (unimodal), so stating it has no mode is NOT true.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following expressions is equal to ∫ (4x³ - 3x⁻⁴ + 5) dx? (C is constant real number)
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Integrating term-by-term:
∫ 4x³ dx = 4 (x⁴/4) = x⁴
∫ -3x⁻⁴ dx = -3 (x⁻³/(-3)) = +x⁻³
∫ 5 dx = 5x
Total integral = x⁴ + x⁻³ + 5x + C.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following statements defines regular polygon?
options: It is a convex polygon with all sides are congruent and the measures of all angles are equal.
It is a simple concave closed curve with all its sides are equal in length.
It is a simple concave closed curve formed by union of three or more line segments.
It is a convex polygon formed by union of three or more-line segments.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: A regular polygon is defined as a convex polygon that is both equilateral (all sides equal in length) and equiangular (all interior angles equal in measure).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Consider the graph of the decreasing exponential function f passing through (-1, 2.5) and (0, 1). Which one of the following represents the graph of f?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
For an exponential function f (x) = aˣ:
f(-1) = a⁻¹ = 2.5 ⇒ a = 1 / 2.5 = 0.4. Then f (x) = (0.4)ˣ = (1 / 2.5)ˣ = (2.5)⁻ˣ.

exam-2018-social-math.text: A point (5, 2) is on a circle, where the center of the circle is (1, -1). Then what is the standard form of equation of the circle?
Which one of the following quantities represents scalar?
options: Force applied to lift damaged car from main road.
The direction and distance moved by a bullet.
Speed of a car observed on speedometer.
The direction of a wind, measured by wind vane.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: A scalar is a physical quantity having magnitude only with no specified direction. Speed (measured by a speedometer) is scalar, whereas force, displacement, and wind direction are vectors.

exam-2018-social-math.text: A contest offers 17 prizes. The first prize is worth Birr 6,000 and each successive prize is worth Birr 300 less than the preceding prize. What is the total value of the prizes in Birr?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
This forms an Arithmetic Progress i on with first term a = 6000, common difference d = -300, and number of terms n = 17. Sum Sₙ = (n/2) * [2a + (n - 1) d]
S₁₇ = (17/2) * [2 (6000) + 16(-300)] = (17/2) * [12000 - 4800] = (17/2) * 7200 = 17 * 3600 = 61,200 Birr.

exam-2018-social-math.text: A company manufactures two products P and Q. Product P requires 2 hours on machine A and 1 hour on machine B. Product Q requires 1 hour on machine A and 1 hour on machine B. Machine A is available for at most 10 hours a day. Machine B is available for at most 8 hours a day. The profit for product P is Birr 40. The profit for product Q is Birr 30. How many units of P and Q should be produced to maximize the profit?
options: 4 units of P and 5 units of Q
10 units of P and 2 units of Q
2 units of P and 6 units of Q
4 units of P and 8 units of Q
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Objective: Maximize Z = 40P + 30Q. Constraints: 2P + Q ≤ 10, P + Q ≤ 8, P ≥ 0, Q ≥ 0. Corner points:
1. (0, 0) ⇒ Z = 0
2. (5, 0) ⇒ Z = 40 (5) = 200
3. (0, 8) ⇒ Z = 30 (8) = 240
4. Intersection of 2P + Q = 10 and P + Q = 8:
Subtracting equations: P = 2, so Q = 8 - 2 = 6. Z (2, 6) = 40 (2) + 30 (6) = 80 + 180 = 260 Birr (Maximum profit). Therefore, producing 2 units of P and 6 units of Q maximizes profit.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
What is the solution of the simultaneous equations:
2x - y = -1
-4x + 3y = 9
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
From equation 1: y = 2x + 1. Substitute into equation 2:
-4x + 3 (2x + 1) = 9 ⇒ -4x + 6x + 3 = 9 ⇒ 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3. Then y = 2 (3) + 1 = 7. Solution is (3, 7).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is the degree of the polynomial function f defined by f (x) = x²(x - 4)(x² + 2)?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
The degree of the product of polynomials is the sum of the degrees of the individual factors:
Degree = 2 + 1 + 2 = 5.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Given a regular square pyramid with base edge 8 cm and slant height 5 cm. What is the total surface area in cm²?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Base area = s² = 8² = 64 cm². Lateral surface area = 4 * (1/2 * base * slant height) = 4 * (1/2 * 8 * 5) = 80 cm². Total Surface Area = Base Area + Lateral Area = 64 + 80 = 144 cm².

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is true about homogeneity of system of linear equations?
options: The system x - 2y - 1 = 0, x + 2y - 3 = 0, x - z + 5 = 0 is homogeneous.
The system x + y = 0, x + 2y + 3z = 0, z = 0 is nonhomogeneous.
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: A system of linear equations Ax = b is defined as homogeneous if and only if all constant terms on the right-hand side are zero (b = 0). System B satisfies this definition identically.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which of the following is equal to Σ(k=1 to 6) (k - 1)²?
Consider a positively skewed frequency curve (tail stretching to the right). Which one of the following is true about the relative position of the measures of central tendency?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: In a positively (right) skewed distribution, extreme high values pull the mean to the far right, so the relationship is always: Mode < Med i an < Mean.

exam-2018-social-math.text: If f (x) = ln (x² + 1) and g (x) = eˣ, then (f ∘ g)'(0) is equal to:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
(f ∘ g)(x) = f (g(x)) = ln((eˣ)² + 1) = ln (e²ˣ + 1). Different i ating with respect to x using the Chain Rule:
(f ∘ g)'(x) = 2e²ˣ / (e²ˣ + 1). Evaluating at x = 0:
(f ∘ g)'(0) = 2e⁰ / (e⁰ + 1) = 2 (1) / (1 + 1) = 2 / 2 = 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the limit of (√(x² - x) - x) as x approaches infinity?

The set of all values of k for which the system of equations:
x + y + z = 1
x + 2y + 4z = k
x + 4y + 10z = k²
is consistent is:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Row reducing the augmented matrix:
[1 1 1 | 1]
[1 2 4 | k]
[1 4 10 | k²]

R2 - R1 → [0, 1, 3 | k - 1]
R3 - R1 → [0, 3, 9 | k² - 1]
R3 - 3*R2 → [0, 0, 0 | (k² - 1) - 3 (k - 1)] = [0, 0, 0 | k² - 3k + 2]. For consistency, the bottom row must have 0 = k² - 3k + 2 ⇒ (k - 1)(k - 2) = 0 ⇒ k = 1 or k = 2. Set of values = {1, 2}.

exam-2018-social-math.text: If u is a vector with initial point (2, 1) and terminal point (-4, 3), then which one of the following is equal to the vector u?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Vector u = (x₂ - x₁) i + (y₂ - y₁) j = (-4 - 2) i + (3 - 1) j = -6i + 2j.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Let f (x) = x / (x² + 3x + 1). Then, f'(x) is equal to:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Using the Quotient Rule: d/dx [u/v] = (u'v - uv') / v²
Here u = x ⇒ u' = 1, v = x² + 3x + 1 ⇒ v' = 2x + 3.
f'(x) = [1 * (x² + 3x + 1) - x * (2x + 3)] / (x² + 3x + 1)²
= (x² + 3x + 1 - 2x² - 3x) / (x² + 3x + 1)² = (1 - x²) / (x² + 3x + 1)².

exam-2018-social-math.text: A shopkeeper wants to increase his profit from Birr 3000 to Birr 3600. By what percent will his profit increase?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Increase = 3600 - 3000 = 600 Birr. Percentage Increase = (600 / 3000) * 100% = 20%.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following sets represents an empty set?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Natural numbers ℕ = {1, 2, 3, 4, ...} are strictly positive integers. There exists no natural number less than or equal to -1. Thus, {x | x ∈ ℕ and x ≤ -1} is the empty set (∅).

exam-2018-social-math.text: Let f (x) = 6x⁶ + 4x⁴ + 3x² + 2 and g (x) = 3x² + 2. Then which one of the following is equal to f (x) / g (x)?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Factoring f (x) by grouping:
f (x) = 2x⁴(3x² + 2) + 1 (3x² + 2) = (2x⁴ + 1)(3x² + 2). Dividing by g (x) = 3x² + 2:
f (x) / g (x) = [(2x⁴ + 1)(3x² + 2)] / (3x² + 2) = 2x⁴ + 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
Let f (x) = 
{ x² - a, if x ≤ 2
{ ax - 2, if x > 2
If f is continuous at x = 2, then the value of a is:
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
For continuity at x = 2:
Left-hand limit = Right-hand limit
2² - a = a (2) - 2 ⇒ 4 - a = 2a - 2 ⇒ 3a = 6 ⇒ a = 2.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the value of the integral from 0 to π of sin³(x) cos (x) dx?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Using substitution: let u = sin (x), then du = cos (x) dx. When x = 0, u = sin (0) = 0. When x = π, u = sin(π) = 0. Integral = ∫₀⁰ u³ du = [u⁴/4]₀⁰ = 0 - 0 = 0.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the sum of the series Σ(n=1 to ∞) 1 / (n (n + 1))?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Using partial fraction decomposition:
1 / [n (n + 1)] = 1/n - 1/(n + 1). The partial sum S_N = (1 - 1/2) + (1/2 - 1/3) + ... + (1/N - 1/(N + 1)) = 1 - 1/(N + 1). Taking the limit as N → ∞:
Sum = lim_{N→∞} [1 - 1/(N + 1)] = 1 - 0 = 1.

exam-2018-social-math.text: The school management wants to study grade eleven students' performance. There are ten sections of grade eleven in the school. Three sections of grade eleven are ran do mly selected and ALL students in these three sections are taken as the sample. Which one of the following is the sampling technique used?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: In cluster sampling, the entire population is divided into natural groups (clusters/sections), a random sample of whole clusters is selected, and every single member within the chosen clusters is surveyed.

exam-2018-social-math.text:
What are the minimum and the maximum values of z = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints:
x + y ≥ 2
x + y ≤ 5
2y - x ≤ 4
x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0
respectively?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation:
Feasible region vertices:
1. (2, 0) ⇒ z = 2 (2) + 3 (0) = 4 (Minimum value) 2. (5, 0) ⇒ z = 2 (5) + 3 (0) = 10
3. Intersection of x + y = 5 and 2y - x = 4: Adding gives 3y = 9 ⇒ y = 3, x = 2 ⇒ (2, 3) ⇒ z = 2 (2) + 3 (3) = 4 + 9 = 13 (Maximum value) 4. (0, 2) ⇒ z = 2 (0) + 3 (2) = 6. Minimum = 4 and Maximum = 13.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following is a convergent series?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: For a geometric series Σ a*r^(k-1) to converge, the absolute value of the common ratio |r| must be strictly less than 1. In D: 2^(k + 1) / 5^(k - 1) = 2² * (2/5)^(k - 1) = 4 * (2/5)^(k - 1). Common ratio r = 2/5 = 0.4 < 1. Therefore, series D converges.

exam-2018-social-math.text: What is the area of a triangle with vertices A (0, 0), B (1, -3) and C (5, 1) (in square units)?
Which one of the following pairs of lines are perpendicular to each other?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: Line 1: y = x - 5 (slope m₁ = 1). Line 2: y = -x + 1 (slope m₂ = -1). Product of slopes: m₁ * m₂ = 1 * (-1) = -1. Therefore, the two lines in A are perpendicular.

exam-2018-social-math.text: Which one of the following logarithmic equations is correctly related with the corresponding exponential equation?
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: By mathematical definition of logarithms: log_a (x) = y is equivalent to the exponential form aʸ = x (with base a > 0, a ≠ 1, x > 0).

exam-2018-social-math.text: For any three sets A, B and C which one of the following is NOT true about the intersection of sets?
options: A ∩ B = A if A ⊆ B
exam-2018-social-math.explanation: The intersection of any set with the empty set is always the empty set: A ∩ ∅ = ∅. Thus, statement B stating A ∩ ∅ = A is false (NOT true).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What is the major difference between practical geography and theoretical geography?
options: Practical geography studies the universe while theoretical studies only Earth.
Practical geography involves field work and applied techniques while theoretical focuses on concepts and models.
Theoretical geography uses field equipment while practical does not.
Practical geography is purely philosophical while theoretical is mathematical.
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Theoretical geography deals with developing geographic concepts, laws, hypotheses, and spatial theories, whereas practical geography applies empirical methods, cartography, GIS, field surveying, and spatial analysis to solve real-world problems.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which early Greek scholar is credited with coining the term 'Geography ' and calculating the Earth' s circumference with remarkable accuracy?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Era tos thenes (c. 276–194 BC) was the chief librarian at Alexandria who coined the word 'Geographia' (earth description) and accurately computed the Earth's circumference using sun angles between Syene and Alexandria.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: During which period did the 'Quantitative Revolution' transform geography into a spatial science using statistical and mathematical models?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Quantitative Revolution in geography occur red during the 1950s and 1960s, shifting geography from descriptive regionalism to rigorous spatial analysis, statistical modeling, and scientific hypothesis testing.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Human Geography from Physical Geography?
options: Human geography studies atmospheric dynamics, whereas physical geography studies urban settlements.
Physical geography is concerned with cultural landscapes, while human geography studies landforms.
Human geography focuses on human societies and their spatial interactions, while physical geography investigates natural processes of the Earth.
There is no functional distinction between human and physical geography.
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Human geography investigates the patterns, processes, and spatial organization of human activities (population, culture, economics, urbanism), while physical geography studies the natural environment (lithosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following is an essential marginal element of a standard map that defines the ratio between map distance and ground distance?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Map scale mathematically expresses the relationship (ratio or proportion) between a given distance measured on the map and the corresponding real distance on the ground.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: On a topographic map, individual features such as water wells, bench marks, and historical monuments are typically represented by:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Cartographic symbols are categorized into point, line, and area symbols. Point symbols represent zero-dimensional geographic locations with fixed coordinates, such as wells, church buildings, spot heights, and monuments.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: If a map has a Represent ative Fraction (R. F.) scale of 1:50,000, what is the actual ground distance represented by a line measuring 4 cm on the map?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: 1 cm on map = 50,000 cm on the ground = 500 meters = 0.5 km. Ground distance = 4 cm * 0.5 km/cm = 2.0 km.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: When contour lines on a topographic map are spaced very close together, they indicate:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Contour lines connect points of equal elevation. When contours are closely packed, elevation changes rapidly over a short horizontal distance, representing a steep slope or cliff.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A direction measured in degrees clock wise starting from True North (000° to 360°) is known as:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: True bearing (whole circle azimuth) is the horizontal angle measured clock wise from True North (0°/360°) to a target line.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What does the acronym GIS stand for in modern geospatial technology?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: GIS stands for Geographic Information System, an integrated frame work for capturing, managing, analyzing, and displaying all forms of geographically referenced spatial and attribute data.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The science and art of gathering data about an object or surface without making physical contact, using sensors on satellites or aircraft, is called:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about the Earth's surface and atmosphere from a distance, typically through electromagnetic radiation sensors mounted on satellites, aircraft, or drones.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Global Positioning System (GPS) determines exact geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude, altitude) by receiving signals from:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: GPS functions by trilaterating radio signals transmitted from a constellation of or biting satellites (minimum 4 satellites in view) to compute precise 3D position coordinates and time.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Earth's lithosphere is comprised of which structural layers?
options: The inner core and outer core
The crust and the uppermost rigid part of the mantle
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid, rigid outer mechanical shell of the Earth, encompassing the entire crust (continental and oceanic) and the brittle upper most mantle, resting above the plastic asthenosphere.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The theory that describes the large-scale motion of seven major and numerous minor lithospheric plates over the asthenosphere is known as:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Plate Tectonics is the unifying geological theory explaining continental drift, sea floor spreading, seismic activity, volcanism, and mountain building through the movement of tectonic plates.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which geological feature is typically formed at divergent plate boundaries where tectonic plates pull apart?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: At divergent (constructive) plate boundaries, extensional forces pull plates apart, creating continental rift valleys (e.g., East African Rift) and mid-ocean ridges (e.g., Mid-Atlantic Ridge) as magma rises to form new crust.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The mechanical disintegration and chemical decomposition of rocks in situ (without major transport) is defined as:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Weathering is the breakdown of rocks, minerals, and soils in place (in situ) through atmospheric, chemical, and biological processes without significant transport.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following processes is a prime example of chemical weathering?
options: Carbonation and oxidation of rock minerals
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition of rocks. Carbon ation (carbonic acid dissolving calcium carbonate in limestone) and oxidation (reaction of iron with oxygen) are prominent chemical weathering processes.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: An oxbow lake is a crescent-shaped water body formed during the old age stage of a river by:
options: River meander neck cut-off and deposition of alluvium
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: As a mature meandering river flows across a flood plain, lateral erosion narrows the meander neck. During high floods, the river cuts through the neck directly, and alluvial deposit i on seals off the abandoned loop, forming an oxbow lake.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following is a classic erosional land form created by alpine glaciation?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Glaciers widen, deepen, and straighten pre-existing river valleys, transforming narrow V-shaped river valleys into steep-sided, flat-bottomed U-shaped valleys (glacial troughs).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following land forms is produced by wind erosion (deflation and abrasion) in arid desert regions?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Yardangs (elongated streamlined ridges) and Zeugen (tabular rock masses under cut by sand blasting) are distinctive erosional land forms created by wind abrasion and deflation in desert environments.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In which layer of the Earth's atmosphere is the ozone layer (O₃) concentrated, absorbing harmful ultraviolet (UV) solar radiation?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The ozone layer is located in the lower stratosphere (approximately 15 to 35 km above sea level), where it absorbs high-energy UV-B and UV-C solar radiation.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The natural atmospheric process that warms the Earth's lower atmosphere by absorbing and re-emitting terrestrial infrared radiation is called the:
