exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The green house effect occurs when atmospheric gases (water vapor, CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) absorb long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation emitted by the Earth, keeping global average surface temperatures hospitable for life.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: As altitude (elevation) above sea level increases, what happens to atmospheric pressure?
options: Atmospheric pressure decreases due to lower air column density.
Atmospheric pressure fluctuates wildly with no relation to elevation.
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the overlying column of air per unit area. As altitude increases, fewer air molecules remain above, causing atmospheric pressure to decrease continuously with height.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Due to the Earth's rotation from west to east, the Coriolis force deflects moving winds and ocean currents:
options: To the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere
To the left in the Northern Hemisphere and to the right in the Southern Hemisphere
Straight towards the poles in both hemispheres
Straight towards the Equator in both hemispheres
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Ferrel's Law states that because of the Coriolis effect, any freely moving object or fluid is deflected to the right of its path in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What does the abbreviation ITCZ stand for in equatorial climatology?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone) is a broad low-pressure belt near the equator where the north east trade winds and south east trade winds converge, producing intense convectional rain fall.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Monsoon winds are fundamentally characterized by:
options: Constant velocity blowing continuously in a single direction throughout the entire year
A complete seasonal reversal in wind direction driven by differential heating of land and sea
Purely localized katabatic mountain breezes occurring at night
Cold polar easterlies circulating only over ice caps
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Monsoons are large-scale seasonal wind systems characterized by a periodic reversal in prevailing wind direction, primarily caused by temperature and pressure differentials between vast continental land masses and adjacent oceans.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The global hydrological cycle is primarily powered by:
options: Earth's magnetic field and tectonic friction
Tidal friction from lunar gravity alone
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The hydrological cycle is driven by solar radiation (which provides energy for evaporation and transpiration) and gravitational force (which causes condensation precipitation, run off, and percolation).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The gently sloping, relatively shallow submerged margin of a continent extending from the coast to the continental slope is called the:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The continental shelf is the shallow under water edge of a continental land mass, averaging less than 200 meters in depth, rich in marine life and off shore mineral/petroleum resources.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: How do warm ocean currents influence the climate of adjacent coastal regions?
options: They create arid coastal deserts with extreme fog.
They lower air temperatures and reduce atmospheric moisture.
They raise coastal air temperatures and increase precipitation and humidity.
They cause perpetual sub-zero freezing along tropical shorelines.
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Warm ocean currents heat the overlying maritime air, boosting evaporation and atmospheric moisture, which leads to higher temperatures and increased rain fall on adjacent coastal lands.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The periodic climatic phenomenon characterized by abnormal warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean is known as:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), characterized by unusual warming of surface waters in the eastern tropical Pacific, disrupting global atmospheric circulation and causing severe droughts or floods world wide.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: According to soil science, which five interrelated factors determine soil formation (pedogenesis)?
options: Magnetism, sunlight, ocean tides, wind speed, latitude
Bedrock hardness, earthquakes, tectonic drift, volcanic ash, glaciers
Human settlement, industrialization, crop rotation, fertilization, irrigation
Parent material, climate, living organisms, topography/relief, and time (CLORPT)
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Hans Jenny's foundational soil equation identifies five primary soil-forming factors: Climate, Organisms, Relief (topography), Parent material, and Time (CLORPT).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In a typical soil profile, which upper most horizon contains the highest concentration of decomposed organic matter (humus) and biological activity?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The O (organic) and A (top soil) horizons sit at the top of the soil profile, rich in decomposed humus, soil microorganisms, plant roots, and essential plant nutrients.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following agricultural practices is widely employed on steep slopes to control surface run off and prevent soil erosion?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Contour plowing (plowing across slopes along contour lines) and terracing (creating stepped flat platforms) significantly reduce run off velocity, promoting water infiltration and preventing severe soil erosion.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The tropical rain forest biome (selva) is distinguished by which combination of environmental characteristics?
options: Year-round high temperatures, heavy rainfall, multi-layered dense canopy, and high biodiversity
Extremely dry conditions, sparse cacti, extreme daily temperature range
Severe sub-zero winters, coniferous pine forests, low annual precipitation
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Tropical rain forest biomes (found along equatorial basins such as the Amazon and Congo) feature high annual temperatures (>24°C), abundant annual rain fall (>2000 mm), stratified multi-canopy ever green trees, and Earth's highest terrestrial biodiversity.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Savanna biome is best described as:
options: An evergreen boreal forest dominated by spruce and fir trees
A frozen desert devoid of vegetative life
A tropical grassland ecosystem with scattered drought-resistant trees, experiencing distinct wet and dry seasons
A temperate deciduous forest with high snowfall in winter
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Savannas are tropical grass land biomes found between tropical wet and semi-arid zones, characterized by tall grasses, scattered acacia and baobab trees, and pronounced wet and dry seasons.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which terrestrial biome is characterized by permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost), short cool summers, and low-growing vegetation such as mosses and lichens?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Arctic and Alpine Tundra biomes are characterized by permafrost, extreme cold, short growing seasons, and dwarf vegetation (lichens, mosses, small sedges).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A biogeographic region characterized by exceptionally high levels of endemic species that is simultaneously under severe threat of habit at destruction is termed a:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Conservation International defines a Biodiversity Hot spot as a region with at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species that has lost at least 70% of its original natural vegetation (such as the Horn of Africa and Eastern Afromontane hot spots).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Large-scale deforestation leads to severe environmental degradation primarily by:
options: Accelerating soil erosion, reducing biodiversity, and increasing atmospheric CO₂ concentrations
Increasing groundwater replenishment and expanding cloud cover
Lowering global temperatures and eliminating river sediment loads
Stabilizing local river discharge throughout dry seasons
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Deforestation strips protective vegetative cover, leading to accelerated run off, severe top soil erosion, habit at destruction, loss of biodiversity, and increased atmospheric CO₂ concentrations.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Ethiopia is located in the Horn of Africa within which approximate latitudinal and longitudinal boundaries?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Astronomically, Ethiopia lies in the tropical zone between approximately 3°N (Moyale) and 14°53 ' N (Bademe) latitude and 32°42 ' E (Akobo) to 47°58 ' E (near Ogaden border) longitude.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The highest mountain peak in Ethiopia, standing at 4,550 meters above sea level in the Simien Mountains, is:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Mount Ras Dashen (4,550 m) in the Simien Mountains National Park is the highest peak in Ethiopia and the fourth highest in Africa.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Great East African Rift Valley divides the Ethiopian highlands into which two major physiographic blocks?
options: The Western plains and Eastern coastal desert
The Northwestern (Western) Highlands and the Southeastern (Eastern) Highlands
The Danakil block and the Ogaden depression
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Ethiopian Rift Valley runs northeast-southwest, cleanly dividing the massive Ethiopian mass ifs into the North western Highlands (Shewan, Gojjam, Gondar, Tigray plate a us) and South eastern Highlands (Arsi, Bale, Hararghe plate a us).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Blue Nile River (Abay) origin ates from which natural water body in the North western Ethiopian Highlands?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Abay (Blue Nile) flows out of the southern end of Lake Tana (fed by the Gilgel Abay) in the Amhara region, before carving deep gorges towards the Sudan border.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which Ethiopian river basin is an endorheic (inland) drainage system that term inates in Lake Abbe on the Djibouti border without reaching any ocean?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Awash River flows entirely within the Ethiopian Rift Valley through middle and lower valleys, term inating in a chain of saline lakes, ending in Lake Abbe on the Ethiopia-Djibouti border.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In the traditional agro-climatic classification of Ethiopia, the 'Kolla' zone corresponds to:
options: Hot lowlands below 1,500 meters altitude with mean temperatures above 20°C
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The traditional Ethiopian agro-climatic zones are: Bereha (<500 m, very hot), Kolla (500–1500 m, warm/hot), Woina Dega (1500–2300 m, temperate), Dega (2300–3300 m, cool), and Wurch/Kur (>3300 m, alpine cold).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The 'Dega' agro-climatic zone in Ethiopia is characterized by which elevation range and agricultural profile?
options: Elevations between 2,300m and 3,300m, cool climate, suitable for barley, wheat, and pulses
Elevations below 500m, desert climate, suitable only for nomadic pastoralism
Elevations between 1,500m and 2,300m, ideal for coffee and teff production
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Dega zone (2300–3300 m) features cool temperatures (10–15°C) and supports high-altitude crops like barley, wheat, faba beans, peas, and high land sheep husbandry.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In Ethiopia, the small rainy season known as 'Belg' typically occurs between:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Belg season (small rains) occurs in spring from March to May, brought by moist south-easterly air masses origin ating from the Indian Ocean.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The main rainy season in Ethiopia ('Kiremt') provides the majority of the annual precipitation from:
options: June to September (Summer), driven by Atlantic and Indian Ocean monsoon winds
December to February (Winter), driven by dry North-Easterly winds
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Kiremt (summer rains) spans June to September, caused by the convergence of moist Guinea monsoon winds (Congo air boundary) and Indian Ocean maritime air as the ITCZ shifts northward over Ethiopia.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which two soil types are dominant and widely cultivated across the Ethiopian volcanic highlands?
options: Nitosols (red volcanic soils) and Vertisols (black clay soils)
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Nitosols (deep, well-drained, fertile red tropical soils) and Vertisols (heavy black cracking clays with high water retention) cover large parts of the Ethiopian plateau and support intensive cereal and coffee agriculture.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Walia Ibex (Capra walie), an iconic endangered wild mammal endemic to Ethiopia, is exclusively found in:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Walia Ibex is strictly endemic to the steep, rocky afro-alpine escarpments of the Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The endangered Ethiopian Wolf (Simien Fox/Canis simensis) has its largest surviving global population concentrated in:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Over half of the world's remaining Ethiopian Wolf population survives in the afro-alpine habit at and Sanetti Plateau of the Bale Mountains National Park.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What is the scientific discipline dedicated to the statistical study of human populations, including size, composition, and spatial distribution?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Demography is the scientific study of human populations, focusing on population dynamics, fertility, mortality, migration, age-sex structures, and geographic distribution.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is defined statistic ally as:
options: The number of children born per woman across her reproductive lifespan
The annual number of live births per 1,000 mid-year total population
The percentage of infant deaths occurring before age one
The ratio of male births to female births
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Crude Birth Rate (CBR) = (Total Live Births in a year / Total Mid-year Population) * 1,000.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In the Demographic Transition Model (DTM), Stage 2 (Early Expanding) is characterized by:
options: High birth rates and high death rates resulting in stationary population
Rapidly falling birth rates and low death rates
High birth rates and rapidly falling death rates, leading to rapid population growth
Birth rates falling below death rates causing population decline
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: In Stage 2 of the DTM, improvements in public health, sanitation, medicine, and food supply drastically reduce death rates while birth rates remain elevated, creating an explosive rate of natural increase.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A population pyramid with a broad base tapering rapidly toward a narrow top indicates:
options: A high birth rate, high youth dependency ratio, and rapid population expansion
An aging population with low fertility rates
Zero population growth with equal proportions across all cohorts
A declining population dominated by senior citizens
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: An expansive (triangular) population pyramid with a broad base reflects high fertility, a high proportion of children under 15 years old, high child dependency, and expanding population momentum (common in developing nations).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The demographic dependency ratio measures the relationship between:
options: The number of emigrants versus immigrants
The urban population versus rural population
The number of literate adults versus illiterate adults
The dependent age groups (0–14 years and 65+ years) and the working-age population (15–64 years)
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Dependency Ratio = [(Population aged 0-14 + Population aged 65+) / Population aged 15-64] * 100.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following is considered a 'Push factor' in human migration?
options: Drought, civil conflict, famine, and lack of employment opportunities
High wages, political stability, and high quality universities
Pleasant climate and advanced healthcare services
Abundant agricultural farmland available for free
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Push factors are unfavorable socio-economic, environmental, or political conditions in a place of origin (e.g., poverty, war, natural disasters, unemployment) that compel individuals to leave.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following is a primary 'Pull factor' attracting rural migrants to metropolitan urban centers?
options: Rural soil erosion and land fragmentation
Lack of clean drinking water in villages
Perception of superior employment prospects, modern education, and healthcare infrastructure
Severe crop failure caused by pests
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Pull factors are positive attributes at a destination (better wages, diverse job markets, educational institutions, modern a men i ties) that attract incoming migrants.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Urbanization refers to:
options: The movement of city residents back to primitive subsistence agriculture
The progressive increase in the percentage and absolute number of people living in urban settlements
The conversion of urban buildings into wildlife conservation parks
The complete decentralization of all manufacturing industries to remote forests
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Urbanization is the demographic, economic, and spatial process by which an increasing proportion of a country's total population becomes concentrated in cities and towns.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A city that is disproportionately larger than any other city in a country (often more than twice as large as the second-ranking city) and dominates national economic and political life is called a:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Mark Jefferson introduced the 'Law of the Primate City', defining a primate city as one that is overwhelmingly the largest in its country, expressing national capacity and culture (e.g., Addis Ababa in Ethiopia).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A rural settlement pattern where houses are constructed in a continuous sequence along a transport ation corridor, river bank, or canal is described as a:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Linear (or ribbon) settlement patterns develop along major physical or transport axes such as roads, railways, coast lines, or river levees for accessibility.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following economic sectors directly extracts raw materials from the Earth's natural environment?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The primary sector encompasses economic activities that directly harvest or extract natural resources from the lithosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The secondary sector of the economy is primarily concerned with:
options: Transforming raw materials into finished manufactured goods through industrial processing
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The secondary economic sector involves value-added manufacturing, construction, energy generation, and industrial processing of primary commodities into manufactured goods.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following activities belongs strictly to the Tertiary sector of an economy?
options: Gold panning in a river bed
Cotton spinning in a textile mill
Tourism hospitality, healthcare services, and retail trade
Wheat harvesting with a combine harvester
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The tertiary sector provides intangible services rather than goods, including transport ation, wholesaling/retailing, tourism, health care, banking, education, and hospitality.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Economic activities centered around information processing, software engineering, biotechnology, and advanced research are classified as:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The quaternary sector represents the knowledge-based component of the economy, including information technology, R&D, financial engineering, scientific consultancy, and strategic management.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Intensive commercial agriculture is characterized by:
options: High inputs of capital, fertilizer, labor, and technology per unit of land area to maximize yields
Large expanses of land with minimal labor input per hectare
Farming solely for household consumption without market sales
Periodic abandonment of agricultural plots through slash-and-burn
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Intensive agriculture maximizes crop yields from a relatively small land area through high capital investment, labor, machinery, fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation inputs.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The traditional agricultural system known as 'shifting cultivation' (swidden or slash-and-burn) involves:
options: Permanent automated greenhouse cultivation in suburbs
Clearing a forest plot by cutting and burning, cultivating for a few years, and moving to a new plot when soil fertility declines
Continuous monocropping on large commercial plantations using heavy combine harvesters
Raising specialized dairy cattle on irrigated pastures
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn) is an extensive subsistence farming system where forest vegetation is cleared and burned to enrich soil with ash; when nutrients deplete after 2-3 years, farmers shift to fallow plots.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The 'Green Revolution' of the mid-20th century substantially boosted global cereal production through the adoption of:
options: Traditional wooden hand-plows and organic manure alone
Genetically modified wild grasses without water irrigation
High-Yielding Variety (HYV) dwarf seeds, synthetic chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and controlled irrigation systems
Complete reliance on natural rainfed subsistence practices
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Pioneered by Nor man Borlaug, the Green Revolution transformed agriculture across Asia and Latin America through modern technology packages consisting of HYVs of wheat/rice, synthetic fertilizers, chemical pest control, and expanded irrigation.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Subsistence agriculture is fundamentally defined as farming that is practiced:
options: Primarily to satisfy the nutritional requirements of the farmer and their family, with little or no surplus for market sale
Exclusively for export to international global commodity markets
By multinational agribusiness conglomerates for corporate profit
On hydroponic factory farms inside urban vertical towers
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Subsistence agriculture produces food crops and livestock primarily for direct domestic consumption by the farming house hold, relying mainly on family labor and simple tools.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Coffee arabica origin ated as a wild indigenous under story tree species in the high land montane rain forests of:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Coffee arabica is native to the south western high land tropical rain forests of Ethiopia (the historical Kaffa region), which holds the highest genetic diversity of wild Arabica coffee on Earth.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which of the following commodities represent the leading agricultural exports generating foreign exchange for Ethiopia?
options: Coffee, oilseeds, pulses, cut flowers, and live animals/meat
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Ethiopia's primary export earnings are generated by high-value agricultural commodities: Arabica coffee (accounting for 30-35%), oil seeds (sesame, niger seed), pulses (chickpeas, beans), floriculture (cut roses), and livestock/meat.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What constitutes the largest untapped and actively developed renewable energy source for electric power generation in Ethiopia?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Due to its rugged topography, deep river canyons, and abundant rain fall, Ethiopia is known as the 'Water Tower of East Africa', possessing an estimated 45,000 MW of exploitable hydroelectric potential.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), the largest hydroelectric power project in Africa, is constructed on which river?
options: Abay (Blue Nile) River in Benishangul-Gumuz Region
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: GERD is a major gravity dam constructed on the Blue Nile (Abay River) in the Guba Wored a of the Benishangul-Gumuz Region, approximately 15 km east of the Sudanese border.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A renewable natural resource is defined as a resource that:
options: Can be replenished or regenerated naturally through physical or ecological cycles over human time scales
Exists in strictly fixed, finite quantities that are permanently depleted once consumed
Can only be created artificially in chemical laboratories
Contains high quantities of radioactive isotopes
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Renewable resources (such as solar radiation, wind energy, water, timber, and biomass) are naturally restored by biogeochemical processes if managed sustainably, in contrast to non-renewable fossil fuels.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The classic Brundtland Commission report (1987) defines 'Sustainable Development' as development that:
options: Focuses exclusively on rapid industrialization without environmental regulations
Halts all technological advancement to preserve raw wilderness unchanged
Meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Prioritizes immediate resource extraction over future resource availability
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Our Common Future (Brundtland Report, 1987) established that sustainable development harmonizes economic growth, social equity, and environmental conservation to safe guard intergenerational equity.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Anthropogenic global climate change and global warming are driven primarily by:
options: Excessive emissions of greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) from fossil fuel burning and land-use change
Underwater volcanic eruptions along deep abyssal trenches
Decreased cosmic ray emissions from distant galaxies
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The scientific consensus shows that human industrial activities—primarily burning coal, oil, and gas, alongside deforestation—have raised atmospheric CO₂ from 280 ppm to over 420 ppm, enhancing the green house effect and driving global warming.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Acid precipitation (acid rain) is produced when industrial emissions of which atmospheric pollutants react with atmospheric water vapor?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Combustion of fossil fuels releases SO₂ and NOₓ gases into the atmosphere, where they oxidize and react with water drop lets to form sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃), causing acid rain (pH < 5.6).

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer was caused primarily by the historical industrial release of:
options: Water vapor from thermal power plants
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons used in refrigeration and aerosols
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: CFCs rise into the stratosphere where UV radiation breaks them down, releasing reactive chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy thousands of ozone molecules, creating the Antarctic ozone hole.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Desert if i cat i on is defined by the United Nations Convention to Combat Desert if i cat i on (UNCCD) as:
options: Land degradation in arid, semi-arid, and dry sub-humid areas resulting from various factors, including climatic variations and human activities
The natural movement of coastal sand dunes by tidal waves
The intentional creation of botanical parks in city centers
Flooding of low-lying plains by torrential rainstorms
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Desert if i cat i on is the pers is tent degradation of dry land ecosystems by overgrazing, deforestation, inappropriate irrigation, and recurring droughts, stripping the biological and economic productivity of land.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The 'Great Green Wall' init i ative in Africa is a pan-continental environmental project designed to:
options: Construct a concrete defensive wall along national borders
Pave green highways connecting North Africa to South Africa
Restore 100 million hectares of degraded land and combat desertification across the Sahel-Sahara belt
Subsidize petroleum exploration in coastal wetlands
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Great Green Wall is an African Union flag ship init i ative stretching 8,000 km across the Sahel from Senegal to Djibouti, planting trees and practicing sustainable land management to combat land degradation and climate change.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Ecotourism is characterized as a form of tourism that:
options: Builds high-rise casinos and mega-malls in pristine national parks
Involves responsible travel to natural areas, conserving the environment, sustaining the well-being of local people, and involving interpretation/education
Encourages trophy hunting of endangered wildlife species
Focuses strictly on industrial factory tours in major metropolitan cities
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Ecotourism promotes low-impact, ecologically sustainable tourism that preserves natural ecosystems, provides direct financial benefits for local community conservation, and educates travelers.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A topographic map portrays three-dimensional land surface relief and elevation differences using:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Contour lines (lines of equal elevation above a datum, usually mean sea level) represent the configuration, slope, and height of the lands cape on a 2D topographic map.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: On a meteorological weather map, a line connecting geographic points that receive equal amounts of rainfall/precipitation over a given period is called an:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: An isohyet is an i so line drawn on a weather map connecting locations that receive equal amounts of precipitation over a designated time period.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: An i so line drawn on a climatological map that connects locations experiencing the same mean atmospheric temperature is termed an:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: An isotherm is a line on a map or chart connecting points having the same temperature at a given time or on average over a given period.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: A line on a weather synoptic chart connecting points of equal atmospheric barometric pressure is known as an:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: I so bars connect points of equal atmospheric pressure (adjusted to sea-level equivalent); closely packed i so bars indicate a steep pressure gradient and high wind speeds.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In satellite remote sensing, 'spatial resolution' refers to:
options: The smallest ground feature size that can be resolved and represented by a single image pixel
The number of spectral bands a sensor can capture
The time it takes for a satellite to orbit the Earth once
The number of bits used to record the digital signal intensity
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Spatial resolution specifies pixel ground dimension (e.g., 30m for Lands at, 10m for Sentinel-2, 0.5m for World View). High spatial resolution resolves smaller objects on the Earth's surface.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In Geographic Information Systems (GIS), the data model that represents spatial geography as a regular matrix of grid cells (pixels) with assigned values is called the:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The raster data model structures continuous spatial phenomena (like satellite imagery, digital elevation models, and land surface temperature) as a continuous matrix of equal-sized rows and columns of grid cells.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In GIS, discrete geographic entities such as roads (lines), city locations (points), and administrative boundaries (polygons) are represented by the:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The vector data model uses explicit coordinate pairs (X, Y) to represent spatial geometries as points (0D), polylines (1D), and polygons/areas (2D) with linked attribute tables.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The cartographic process of simplifying, selecting, smoothing, and aggregating detailed geographic features to maintain clarity when reducing map scale is called:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Cartographic generalization simplifies real-world complexities so that a smaller-scale map remains legible, visually balanced, and functionally informative without over crowding.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which category of map projection is best suited for mapping mid-latitude regions with predominantly east-west territorial elongation (such as the United States or Europe)?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Conic map projections conceptualize projecting the Earth onto a tangent or secant cone, minimizing distortion along standard parallels in mid-latitude zones with broad east-west extents.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What is the primary cartographic distortion inherent in the standard cylindrical Mercator projection?
options: Shapes are completely distorted at the Equator.
Area is severely exaggerated at high latitudes towards the poles (e.g., Greenland appears larger than Africa).
Compass navigation rhumb lines are plotted as complex spiral curves.
Distances along the Equator are reduced to zero.
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: While the Mercator projection is conformal (preserving local angles and compass bearings for maritime navigation), its area scale increases infinitely towards the poles, vastly exaggerating the size of high-latitude land masses.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Physiographically, the Ethiopian land mass is divided into Highlands and Low lands based on which conventional elevation contour threshold?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: In Ethiopian geography, land above the 1,500-meter contour line is defined as Highlands (High Plateau accounting for ~56% of the country), while land below 1,500 meters constitutes the Low lands.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Main Ethiopian Rift (MER) was formed by which tectonic mechanism?
options: Tensional tectonic stress pulling the African and Arabian plates apart, causing crustal rifting and graben subsidence
Glacial erosion scouring deep bedrock trenches
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Extensional tectonic forces driven by mantle plumes pulled the Nubian and Somalian sub-plates apart, faulting the Earth's crust along parallel faults and forming the subsiding central rift graben.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Danakil (Afar) Depression in north eastern Ethiopia is globally renowned for which unique geographic features?
options: Dense tropical rainforests with heavy annual snowfall
Alpine glacial tarns located at 4,000 meters above sea level
Perennial sub-zero temperatures and tundra vegetation
Being one of the hottest places on Earth, containing areas below sea level (Kobar Sink at -125m) and active shield volcanoes like Erta Ale
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: The Danakil Depression is a hyper-arid tectonic triple junction containing the Kobar Sink (-125 m below sea level), geothermal sulfur springs at Dallol, and the continuously active lava lake of Erta Ale volcano.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: Which agricultural commodity remains the dominant single source of foreign exchange revenue for Ethiopia?
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Coffee is Ethiopia's most valuable export crop, generating over $1.3 billion annually and supporting the livelihoods of an estimated 15 million citizens across the supply chain.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The settlement distribution in the Ethiopian Highlands is historically characterized by:
options: Dense coastal ports and seaside canal towns
Dispersed homesteads and nucleated hilltop villages situated to avoid malaria-prone lowlands
Nomadic tent encampments following desert dunes
Subterranean cave complexes below sea level
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Due to favorable temperate climate, reliable rain fall, and freedom from tropical diseases (like malaria and trypanosomiasis), over 80% of Ethiopia's population settled in high land village mass ifs.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In Ethiopia, agro-ecological zoning is primarily determined by the interaction between which two dominant geographic variables?
options: Soil salinity and ocean tidal currents
Wind vane azimuth and barometric tide
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Altitude heavily modifies temperature (lapse rate) and rain fall patterns across Ethiopia's complex terrain, serving as the foundational determinant of agro-ecological zones and cropping systems.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: What is the most severe and widespread environmental land degradation challenge affecting agricultural productivity in the Ethiopian Highlands?
options: Severe soil erosion and loss of fertile topsoil caused by steep slopes, deforestation, and heavy rains
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: High population pressure, steep cultivated slopes, loss of tree canopy, and torrential monsoon downpours cause massive top soil erosion, costing Ethiopia billions of tons of fertile soil annually.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The Sustainable Land Management Program (SLMP) implemented across various Ethiopian regional states focuses on:
options: Clearing all natural forests to expand urban cement factories
Community-based integrated watershed management, physical soil bunds, terracing, and re-vegetation
Constructing thermal coal power plants in wildlife sanctuaries
Converting highland rivers into artificial saltwater lakes
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: SLMP is a nation wide init i ative promoting sustainable land management through community water shed rest or ation, biological stabilization, check dams, stone/soil bunds, and agroforestry.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: The ran king and structural organization of human settlements in a country according to population size, economic functions, and service sphere of influence is known as the:
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: An urban hierarchy classifies urban centers into hierarchical tiers (hamlet, village, town, regional city, national primate city) based on population threshold, functional complexity, and central place services.

exam-2018-social-geog.text: In contemporary economic geography, 'Globalization' refers to:
options: The complete isolation of national economies behind impenetrable trade barriers
The restriction of all cultural communication to local tribal dialects
The increasing interconnectedness, integration, and interdependence of world economies, cultures, financial markets, and technologies across international borders
The elimination of global shipping networks in favor of horse carts
exam-2018-social-geog.explanation: Globalization is the on going process of accelerating world wide interconnectedness and integration across economies, trade, capital flows, information technology, and cultural exchange.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which of the following sources of historical knowledge provides primary, first-hand evidence created at the time of the event under study?
options: Eyewitness accounts, original manuscripts, archival documents, and archaeological artifacts
Modern historical textbooks and encyclopedias written centuries later
Fictional novels and dramatized television series
Secondary analysis articles and peer-reviewed commentaries
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Primary sources are direct, contemporary evidence from the period being studied, including original government records, inscriptions, letters, diaries, oral accounts by eye witnesses, and excavated archaeological art if acts.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The world-famous hominid fossil 'Lucy' (locally known in Amharic as 'Dinknesh') was discovered in 1974 by Donald Johanson and his team at which paleoanthropological site in Ethiopia?
options: Melka Kunture in the Awash valley
Porc Epic cave near Dire Dawa
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Australopithecus afarensis fossil AL 288-1 ('Lucy ' or ' Dinknesh'), dated to 3.2 million years old and demonstrating habitual bipedalism, was excavated at Hadar in the lower Awash River Valley, Afar region, in November 1974.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The fossil specimen of Australopithecus afarensis ('Lucy' / 'Dinknesh') lived approximately how many years ago?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Radiometric dating of volcanic ash layers embedding the Hadar fossil stratigraphy established Lucy's age at approximately 3.18 to 3.2 million years before present (Pliocene epoch).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 'Neolithic Revolution' in world history is fundamentally characterized by:
options: The manufacture of iron steam engines and railways
The discovery of fire and nomadic hunting-gathering
The transition from nomadic foraging to plant domestication, animal husbandry, and sedentary village settlements
The mass migration of Homo erectus out of Africa
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Neolithic Revolution (New Stone Age, c. 10,000 BCE) marked the pivotal agricultural transition from for aging to food production (domestic ation of wheat, barley, teff, enset, cattle), enabling permanent settlements, pottery, and social complexity.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which ancient civilization developed along the fertile flood plains of the Nile River in north eastern Africa, renowned for hieroglyphic writing, pharaonic dynasties, and monumental pyramids?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Ancient Egypt flour i shed along the lower reaches of the Nile River, developing one of humanity's earliest centralized states, monumental architecture (Giza pyramids), papyrus writing, and complex religious institutions.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The ancient land of Punt, renowned in ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic inscriptions for rich trade in myrrh, frankincense, gold, ebony, and ivory, was located in:
options: The Horn of Africa (coastal Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Somalia)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Egyptian expedition records (not a bly Queen Hatshepsut's 15th-century BC Deir el-Bahari relief) describe maritime expeditions to the 'Land of Punt' situated along the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden coasts in the Horn of Africa.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The pre-Aksumite Kingdom of Da'amat (Damot), which flour i shed in northern Ethiopia during the first millennium BCE, had its major religious and architectural center at:
options: Yeha (famed for the Temple of the Moon)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Kingdom of Da'amat (fl. 8th–5th centuries BCE) had its ceremonial and political center at Yeha in Tigray, featuring South Arabian-influenced epigraphic inscriptions and the surviving limestone Temple of the Moon.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: What was the principal international maritime port city of the Kingdom of Aksum on the Red Sea coast, linking the Ethiopian highlands with the Greco-Roman, Indian, and Byzantine worlds?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Adulis (situated on the Gulf of Zula near modern Massawa) was the chief commercial port of the Aksumite Empire, recorded extensively in the 1st-century CE Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: King Ezana of Aksum converted to Christianity during the mid-4th century AD (c. 330–340 AD) through the evangelization of which Christian scholar who be came the first Bishop (Abba Salama) of Ethiopia?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Frumentius, a consecrated Tyrian scholar, tutored Ezana and was later ordained as the first Metropolitan Bishop of Aksum by Patriarch At hanas i us of Alexandria in Egypt, adopting the honorary title Abba Salama ('Father of Peace').

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Islam was first introduced into Ethiopia during the life time of Prophet Muhammad when early Muslim converts fled persecution in Mecca in 615 AD in what is known as the:
options: First Hijra (migration) to the Aksumite Kingdom ruled by King Armah (Al-Najashi)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In 615 AD, facing violent persecution in Mecca, Prophet Muhammad instructed his followers to seek asylum in the Christian Kingdom of Aksum, where King Armah (Al-Najashi) granted them sanctuary and religious freedom (First Hijra).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Zagwe Dynasty, which succeeded the Aksumite state in the 12th century, established its imperial capital at Roha (modern Lalibela) in the province of:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Agaw-speaking Zagwe Dynasty arose in the Lasta mountains of northern Wollo, shifting the political and ecclesiastical center of the Ethiopian Christian state southwards to Roha.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The world-famous monolithic rock-hewn churches of Lalibela (including Bete Giyorgis and Bete Medhane Alem) were excavated during the reign of which Zagwe monarch?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: King Lalibela (reigned c. late 12th - early 13th century) commissioned the carving of eleven monolithic and semi-monolithic rock-hewn churches out of solid volcanic tuff to establish a 'New Jerusalem' in Lasta.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In 1270 AD, the Zagwe dynasty ended and the 'Solomonic Dynasty' was restored in Shewa under the leader ship of:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Yekuno Amlak defeated the last Zagwe King Yetbarak in 1270 AD with the political backing of Saint Tekle Haymanot and the Shewan Amhara nobility, proclaiming genealogical descent from King Solomon and Queen of Sheba.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Emperor Amda Seyon I (reigned 1314–1344) is celebrated in Ethiopian medieval history for:
options: Surrendering all highland territories to foreign invaders
Moving the imperial capital permanently to Massawa
Major military campaigns that consolidated Christian imperial hegemony over Muslim coastal sultanates and southern regions
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Amda Seyon I expanded the borders of the medieval Christian kingdom through military campaigns, subduing the Muslim sultanates of Ifat, Hadya, Dawaro, and Bale, and establishing a dominant tributary empire.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Sultanates of Ifat and Adal were prominent medieval Islamic polities that developed primarily along which lucrative commercial corridor?
options: The eastern trade routes connecting the fertile central Ethiopian highlands to the Gulf of Aden port of Zeila
The Atlantic slave trade routes along the Congo river
The trans-Saharan caravan network across the Sahara desert
The southern Mediterranean maritime shipping lanes
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Walashma dynasty of Ifat and later Adal control led the strategic Zeila trade route, channeling high land ivory, gold, spices, and coffee to Arabian and Indian Ocean merchant networks.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 16th-century armed conflict between the Christian High land Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal (1529–1543) was led on the Muslim side by which military commander?
options: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (Ahmad Gragn)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi ('Ahmad Gragn ' or ' the Left-Handed') led the armies of Adal armed with Ottoman fire arms, defeating Emperor Lebna Dengel at the Battle of Shimbra Kure in 1529 and ruling the highlands for 14 years.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: A Portuguese military expedition of 400 musketeers arrived in 1541 to aid the Christian Kingdom against Imam Ahmad Gragn, commanded by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Cristóvão da Gama (son of Vasco da Gama) led the 400 Portuguese soldiers who reinforced Emperor Galawdewos, culminating in the Battle of Wayna Daga in 1543 where Imam Ahmad was killed.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 16th-century Oromo population movement and expansion across the Ethiopian plateau was socio-politically organized and regulated by which indigenous institution?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Gadaa system—with its organized 8-year age-grade leader ship (Abba Gadaa and military leader Abba Duula)—provided the social cohesion, military mobilization, and governance structure that facilitated the 16th-century Oromo expansion.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Oromo 'Gadaa System' is best defined as:
options: A hereditary military dictatorship ruled by absolute kings
A monastic religious order dedicated exclusively to scriptural translation
A trade guild of maritime merchants along the Red Sea
An indigenous democratic system of socio-political administration based on generation classes with peaceful power transfer every eight years
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Her it age, Gadaa is an egalitarian, democratic governance system where male cohorts advance through 8-year grades (Gadaa classes), transfer ring political, judicial, and legislative power every 8 years.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Gondarine Period in Ethiopian history was init i ated in 1636 when which emperor established Gondar as the permanent imperial capital?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: After expelling Jesuit missionaries and restoring Orthodox Christianity in 1632, Emperor Fasilides ended centuries of roving royal tent camps by establishing Gondar as the permanent imperial capital in 1636.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The architectural marvel of Gondar, the 'Fasil Ghebbi' (Royal Enclosure), is distinguished by:
options: Stone castle complexes and palaces blending indigenous Aksumite, Portuguese, Arab-Moorish, and Indian architectural styles
Mud-brick sun-dried adobe huts with thatched roofs
Pre-fabricated cast iron and glass modern skyscrapers
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Fasil Ghebbi encompasses fortified stone castles, battlements, banquet halls, and libraries built by consecutive Gondarine monarchs (Fasilides, Yohannes I, Iyasu I, Bakaffa, Empress Mentewab) displaying unique synthesis of diverse building traditions.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 'Era of the Princes' (Zemene Mesafint) in Ethiopian history was triggered in 1769 when Ras Mikael Sehul of Tigray assassinated/deposed which puppet Gondarine emperor?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In 1769, Ras Mikael Sehul assassin ated Emperor Iyoas I and placed elderly Yohannes II on the throne, reducing the monarchy to figure heads and inaugurating the century of regional war lord fragment ation (Zemene Mesafint).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which of the following was a defining political characteristic of the Zemene Mesafint (1769–1855)?
options: Decentralization of political power, autonomous regional warlords (Rases), powerless puppet emperors in Gondar, and chronic civil war
A highly centralized bureaucratic empire dominated by a single despotic emperor
Foreign British colonial military occupation throughout the entire interior
A peaceful democratic parliament with universal suffrage
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: During the Zemene Mesafint (1769–1855), powerful regional lords of Begemder, Tigray, Gojjam, Wollo, and Shewa competed for the title of End erase (Regent), reducing the imperial crown to symbolic status amid continuous civil strife.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The end of the Zemene Mesafint and the beginning of modern Ethiopian state centralization was marked in 1855 by the coronation of:
options: Emperor Tewodros II (Kassa Hailu of Qwara)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Kassa Hailu defeated rival regional feudal lords in battles at Gur Amba, Gorgora Bichen, Ayshal, and Deresge, and was crowned Emperor Tewodros II in February 1855, launching ambitious national unif i cat i on and administrative reforms.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The tragic demise of Emperor Tewodros II occur red in April 1868 at which mountain fortress following the British military expedition commanded by Sir Robert Napier?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: After Napier's British-Indian expedition breached the Meqdela mountain fortress on April 13, 1868, Emperor Tewodros II committed suicide with his pistol rather than surrender to foreign forces.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Emperor Yohannes IV (reigned 1872–1889) successfully defended Ethiopian sovereignty against external invasions in the 1870s by decisively defeating the expansionist Egyptian forces at:
options: The Battles of Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Khedive Ismail of Egypt dispatched modern armies under European and American mercenary officers to annex northern Ethiopia, but Yohannes IV and Ras Alula decimated them at Gundet (Nov 1875) and Gura (March 1876).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The religious council convened by Emperor Yohannes IV in 1878 to resolve deep theological disputes within the Ethiopian Orthodox Church and enforce doctrinal uniformity was held at:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: At the Council of Boru Meda (1878), Yohannes IV declared the Tewahdo (Unionist) doctrine as the sole orthodox doctrine of the Church, banning the rival Sost Lidet and Qebat sects, and requiring Muslim leaders in Wollo to convert.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Emperor Yohannes IV died on the battle field in March 1889 fighting against the invading Mahdist forces of Sudan at the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On March 9, 1889, while leading the Ethiopian army to victory over Mahdist Sudanese forces at the Battle of Metemma, Yohannes IV was struck by a sniper bullet and died the following day.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: During his reign, Emperor Menelik II (1889–1913) carried out extensive territorial integration that shaped modern Ethiopia by:
options: Incorporating the southern, southwestern, and eastern kingdoms and principalities into the centralized Ethiopian state
Ceding all highland territories to European colonial empires
Dismantling the national postal and communication network
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Menelik II expanded southwards, westwards, and eastwards (incorporating Gurage, Arsi, Wolayta, Kaffa, Harar, Jimma, Somali, Gambella, and Benishangul regions), forging modern Ethiopia's recognized territorial boundaries.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The diplomatic dispute between Ethiopia and Italy that directly caused the First Italo-Ethiopian War arose from conflicting translations of which Article in the 1889 Treaty of Wuchale?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In the Amharic text of Article XVII, Ethiopia 'could' choose to use Italian diplomatic channels for foreign relations (optional), while the Italian text stated Ethiopia 'consented' to use Italy (obligatory protectorate), prompting Menelik II to abrogate the treaty.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: On March 1, 1896, the Ethiopian army led by Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu Betul achieved a historic victory over invading Italian colonial forces at the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: At the Battle of Adwa (Sunday, March 1, 1896), the Ethiopian united army crushed General Oreste Baratieri's four Italian brigades, inflicting over 6,000 casual ties and decisively defending national independence.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: What was the profound global and African significance of the Ethiopian victory at the Battle of Adwa (1896)?
options: It led directly to the total colonization of Ethiopia by Great Britain.
It caused Ethiopia to renounce all modern diplomatic ties with foreign nations.
It was the first decisive military defeat of a major European colonial empire by an African nation, inspiring Pan-African liberation movements globally
It forced Italy to annex all Red Sea coastal territories permanently.
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Adwa shattered the myth of European racial and military invincibility, secured Ethiopia's sovereign international recognition, and stood as an enduring beacon of freedom for Pan-African and anti-colonial movements across the globe.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which of the following modern technological innovations was introduced to Ethiopia during the reign of Emperor Menelik II?
options: The Ethio-Djibouti railway, telegraph/telephone systems, Bank of Abyssinia, Menelik II School, and Menelik II Hospital
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Menelik II modern ised Ethiopia by founding Addis Ababa (1886), constructing the Franco-Ethiopian railway to Djibouti, establishing modern postal/telecom networks, printing national currency, opening the Bank of Abyssinia (1905), and building first state schools and hospitals.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Lij Iyasu (designated heir of Menelik II who ruled from 1913 to 1916) was deposed in September 1916 primarily because of:
options: His refusal to collect any taxes from the nobility
Opposition from Shewan feudal nobility and Allied powers who accused him of aligning with Islam and the Central Powers during World War I
His surrender to Italian colonial forces in Massawa
His decision to move the capital back to Gondar
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Lij Iyasu attempted progressive national integration by appointing Muslim leaders, building mosques, and fostering ties with Somali leader Sayyid Muhammad Abdullah Hass an and the Ottoman Empire, which alarmed Orthodox clergy, Shewan nobility, and Allied legations (Britain, France, Italy).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Following the coup d'état of September 1916, who was crowned Empress of Ethiopia with Ras Teferi Mekonnen appointed as Regent and Heir to the Throne?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Empress Zewditu was crowned as the first female head of state of modern Ethiopia (reigned 1916–1930) in a diarchical power arrangement, while Ras Teferi Mekonnen directed state administration and modernization.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Under the diplomatic leader ship of Regent Ras Teferi Mekonnen, Ethiopia gained international recognition by officially joining the League of Nations in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In September 1923, Ethiopia was formally admitted to the League of Nations in Geneva, strengthening diplomatic sovereignty and committing to the progressive eradication of the slave trade.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: On November 2, 1930, Ras Teferi Mekonnen was formally crowned Emperor of Ethiopia under which regal throne name?
options: Emperor Haile Selassie I ('Power of the Trinity')
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Following Empress Zewditu's death, Negus Teferi was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I ('Power of the Holy Trinity', King of Kings of Ethiopia, Conquering Lion of the Tribe of Judah) at St. George Cathedral in Addis Ababa on November 2, 1930.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Ethiopia's first written constitution, introduced by Emperor Haile Selassie I to modernize central government and consolidate absolute imperial power, was promulgated in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The 1931 Constitution established a bicameral parliament (Chamber of Deputies and Senate) while legally enshrining supreme absolute authority in the person of the Emperor and establishing hereditary dynastic success i on.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The border skirmish engineered by Fascist Italy in December 1934 to manufacture a pretext for the 1935 invasion of Ethiopia was the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On December 5, 1934, Italian colonial troops occupying an illegal fort at Walwal inside Ethiopia clashed with Ethiopian escort forces, providing Benito Mussolini the manufactured crisis to invade in October 1935.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: During the five-year Italian Fascist occupation (1936–1941), Ethiopian resistance was valiantly sustained across the country by guerrilla fighters known as:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Arbegnoch (Patriotic resistance fighters), led by leaders like Ras Abebe Aregai, Belay Zeleke, Amoraw Wubneh, and Shewareged Gedle, waged an unyielding guerrilla resistance against Fascist military rule.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: On May 5, 1941, Emperor Haile Selassie I triumphantly re-entered Addis Ababa, ending the five-year Italian occupation, aided by Ethiopian Patriots and British/Allied forces known as:
options: Gideon Force (commanded by Orde Wingate and Dan Sandford)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Gideon Force, a British-Ethiopian special guerrilla brigade under Major Orde Wingate accompanying Emperor Haile Selassie, fought alongside northern Patriots, culminating in the liberation of Addis Ababa on May 5, 1941.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In 1952, under United Nations General Assembly Resolution 390 A (V), Eritrea was officially reunited with Ethiopia under which constitutional structure?
options: An autonomous unit federated under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian Crown
A direct military protectorate of Italy
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The UN Federation of 1952 granted Eritrea internal self-government (with its own constitution, parliament, and police force) while placing defense, foreign affairs, currency, and international commerce under the Ethiopian Federal Crown.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In December 1960, while Emperor Haile Selassie was visiting Brazil, a progressive military coup d'état was launched against the feudal imperial regime led by:
options: Brigadier General Mengistu Neway (Imperial Bodyguard commander) and his brother Girmame Neway
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Neway brothers mobilized the Imperial Body guard (Kebur Zabagna) in December 1960 to over throw the feudal aristocracy and declare Crown Prince Asfaw Wossen constitutional monarch before the coup was crushed by the regular army.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In the late 1960s and early 1970s, the radical Ethiopian Student Movement (ESM) mobilized widespread civil opposition against imperial autocracy under which iconic slogan?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: First articulated by student leader Ibsa Gutama and university activists in 1965, 'Land to the Tiller' (Meret Le-Arashu) demanded the abolition of exploit ative tenant-landlord feudal relations, becoming the catalyst for the 1974 revolution.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: On September 12, 1974, the centuries-old Solomonic imperial monarchy in Ethiopia came to an end when Emperor Haile Selassie I was deposed by the military committee known as:
options: The Derg (Provisional Military Administrative Council - PMAC)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Derg (Ge 'ez for ' Committee', comprising 108 junior military and police officers) arrested and deposed Emperor Haile Selassie on September 12, 1974, establishing military socialist rule under the slogan 'Ethiopia Tikdem'.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Who emerged as the undisputed autocratic military dictator of the Derg regime and head of state of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (PDRE)?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Through a series of internal purges (eliminating rivals Aman Andom, Teferi Benti, and Atnafu Abate), Mengistu Haile Mariam consolidated absolute power as Derg Chairman and later General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Ethiopia (WPE).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In March 1975, the Derg enacted which radical socialist proclamation that fundamentally transformed the rural socio-economic lands cape of Ethiopia?
options: The privatization of all state banks
Proclamation No. 31/1975: The Public Ownership of Rural Lands (abolishing private land ownership and tenancy)
The re-establishment of feudal Gult estates
The immediate return of lands to the imperial family
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Proclamation No. 31 of March 1975 nationalized all rural lands without compensation, banned the hiring of wage labor and land mortgaging, distributed land up to 10 hectares per farming family, and established Peasant Associations (Kebele).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The violent urban counter-insurgency campaign waged by the Derg regime in 1977–1978 to eliminate civilian political opposition (not a bly the EPRP) is known as the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Red Terror (Qey Shibir) was an urban terror campaign executed by the Derg security apparatus and Kebele militias, resulting in the extrajudicial detention, torture, and killing of tens of thousands of educated youths and political activists.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: During the 1977–1978 Ethio-Somali War (Ogaden War), the invasion launched by Somali President Siad Barre was defeated by Ethiopian armed forces with direct military assistance from:
options: The Soviet Union (USSR), Cuba, and South Yemen
The United States and Great Britain
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In a Cold War alignment shift, the USSR delivered $1 billion in heavy armaments (tanks, MiG-21/23 jets) alongside 15,000 combat troops deployed by Cuba under General Arnaldo Ochoa to help Ethiopia repel the Somali army at Harar and Karamara (March 1978).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 17-year rule of the military Marxist Derg regime collapsed on May 28, 1991 when which coalition captured Addis Ababa?
options: The Ethiopian Peoples' Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF)
The League of Nations peacekeeping force
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Following Mengistu's flight to Zimbabwe on May 21, 1991, EPRDF forces entered Addis Ababa on May 28, 1991, concluding the civil war and establishing the Transitional Government of Ethiopia (TGE).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 'Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade' (16th to 19th centuries) formed a triangular trading system connecting which three continents?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Triangular Trade transported European manufactured goods (guns, textiles) to Africa, enslaved Africans across the Middle Passage to plant ation colonies in the Americas, and raw agricultural commodities (sugar, tobacco, cotton) back to Europe.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Industrial Revolution, which transitioned human manufacturing from manual hand crafts to steam-powered factory mechanization, origin ated during the mid-18th century in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Britain pioneered the Industrial Revolution (c. 1760–1840) due to rich coal and iron deposits, agricultural productivity gains, financial capital, patent protection, and mechanization in textile spinning and James Watt's steam engine.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The French Revolution of 1789 abolished feudal absolute monarchy under which world-renowned revolutionary rallying slogan?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The French Revolution dismantled the Ancien Régime and promulgated the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen under the tripartite ideal of 'Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité' (Liberty, Equality, Fraternity).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885, which laid down the ground rules for the colonial 'Scramble for Africa', was convened by which German Chancellor?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck convened 14 European powers and the USA at the Berlin Conference (1884–85), enacting the 'Principle of Effective Occupation' to part ition Africa without armed European conflict.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which European colonial power primarily implemented the colonial administrative policy of 'Direct Rule ' and ' Assimilation' (attempting to turn colonized subjects into French citizens)?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: France employed centralized Direct Rule and the cultural policy of Assimilation (and later Association), placing French commandants over administrative cercles and requiring Africans to adopt French language and law to attain citizenship.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The British colonial administrative doctrine of 'Indirect Rule', governing through indigenous traditional chiefs and customary native courts, was formulated by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Lord Lugard formulated 'Indirect Rule' in The Dual Man date in British Tropical Africa, utilizing pre-existing traditional hierarchical structures (such as Fulani emirs in Northern Nigeria) to enforce colonial tax ation and law at minimal British administrative cost.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which two African nations successfully maintained their political independence during the 19th-century European 'Scramble for Africa'?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Throughout the Scramble for Africa, only Ethiopia (through decisive military victory at Adwa in 1896) and Liberia (established by free African Americans in 1847 under US diplomatic patronage) preserved sovereign independence.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The out break of World War I in July 1914 was sparked by the assassin ation of Arch duke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, in Sarajevo by:
options: Gavrilo Princip (a Bosnian Serb nationalist of the Black Hand)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On June 28, 1914, 19-year-old Gavrilo Princip shot Arch duke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo, triggering the diplomatic July Crisis and interlocking European military alliances into World War I.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Treaty of Versailles (1919), which formally concluded World War I, imposed severe financial reparations, territorial losses, and the 'War Guilt Clause' (Article 231) on:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Versailles Treaty forced Germany to accept sole moral responsibility for WWI, pay massive financial reparations, surrender Alsace-Lorraine and over seas colonies, demilitarize the Rhineland, and drastically cap its military size.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Bolshevik Revolution of October/November 1917 in Russia, which overthrew the Russian Provisional Government and established the world's first socialist state, was led by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik party to seize power in Petrograd under the slogans 'All Power to the Soviets ' and ' Peace, Land, and Bread', founding Soviet Russia.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: World War II in Europe was officially triggered on September 1, 1939 when Nazi Germany under Adolf Hitler launched a Blitzkrieg invasion of:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Hitler's unprovoked invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939 compelled Britain and France to honor their defense guarantees by declaring war on Germany on September 3, starting World War II.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The state-sponsored, systematic genocide perpetrated by Nazi Germany during World War II that murdered six million European Jews and millions of others is known as:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Holocaust was the industrialized genocide or chest rated by Nazi Germany (1941–1945), murdering two-thirds of European Jewry alongside Romani people, Soviet prisoners of war, and disabled individuals in concentration and death camps.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The United Nations (UN) was established in 1945 to maintain international peace and security at the San Francisco Conference following the end of:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The UN Charter was signed on June 26, 1945 in San Francisco by 50 nations (including Ethiopia as an original founding member) to replace the failed League of Nations and prevent future global warfare.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 'Cold War' (1947–1991) is characterized as an ideological, geopolitical, and military rivalry between which two superpowers?
options: The United States (leading the capitalist Western bloc) and the Soviet Union (leading the communist Eastern bloc)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Cold War pitted the USA (democracy/capitalism/NATO) against the USSR (Marxism-Leninism/Warsaw Pact) in an era of nuclear arms race, space exploration rivalry, and proxy wars across Korea, Vietnam, and Africa without direct superpower warfare.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The year 1960 is celebrated as the 'Year of Africa' in world history because:
options: All African economies adopted a single common currency
European colonial powers colonized the entire continent anew
Seventeen African nations achieved sovereign independence from colonial rule in that single year
The African Union was established in Cairo
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In 1960, seventeen newly independent African countries (including Nigeria, DRC, Cameroon, Senegal, Ivory Coast, and Somalia) gained independence, marking the decisive break through of continental decolonization.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) was founded on May 25, 1963 with its permanent head quarters established in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Thirty-two independent African heads of state met in Addis Ababa under the host chairman ship of Emperor Haile Selassie I on May 25, 1963, signing the OAU Charter and designating Addis Ababa as the permanent diplomatic capital of Africa.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The institutionalized racial segregation and white minority supremacy system in South Africa known as 'Apartheid' was dismantled in 1994 with the election of:
options: Nelson Mandela (leader of the African National Congress)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Following decades of armed and civil struggle and 27 years of imprisonment, Nelson Mandela won South Africa's first multiracial democratic elections in April 1994, becoming the nation's first Black president and dismantling Apartheid.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The dissolution and collapse of the Soviet Union (USSR), marking the end of the Cold War, occur red in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Following Mikhail Gorbachev's Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring) policies, the 15 Soviet Republics declared independence, and the USSR officially dissolved on December 26, 1991.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The earliest known stone tool technology manufactured by early hominids (Homo habilis), consisting of simple chipped river pebbles and chop pers, is known as the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Oldowan stone tool culture (dating from 2.6 to 1.7 million years ago, named after Olduvai Gorge and found at Gona in Afar) represents humanity's oldest archaeological tool industry.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The ancient Babylonian legal code compiled around 1750 BCE, inscribed on a diorite stele and renowned for the principle of retributive justice ('an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth'), is the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: King Hammurabi of Babylon codified 282 legal statutes governing property, contracts, family law, and criminal punishments, exemplifying the ancient legal doctrine of Lex Talionis.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Which ancient Greek city-state (Polis) is renowned as the birth place of Western direct democracy, philosophical inquiry (Socrates, Plato), and classical drama?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Under states men like Cleisthenes and Pericles (5th century BCE), classical A thens instituted direct citizen assembly democracy (Ecclesia) and gave birth to Western philosophy, theater, and arts.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The two-century period of relative peace, imperial expansion, and economic stability across the Roman Empire init i ated under Emperor August us is known as the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Pax Romana (Roman Peace, 27 BCE – 180 CE) spanned from the reign of August us to Marcus Aurelius, characterized by minimal civil expansion warfare, extensive road building, and flour is hing trade across the Mediterranean basin.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Magna Carta (Great Charter), signed by King John of England at Runnymede in 1215, was historically momentous because it:
options: Gave the king unlimited power to execute citizens without trial
Established the principle that the monarch is subject to the rule of law and protected feudal barons from arbitrary royal imprisonment (habeas corpus)
Abolished all taxes in the Kingdom of England
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Magna Carta (1215) forced the English Crown to acknowledge legal constraints on royal prerogative, guaranteeing due process of law and laying the found ation for modern constitutional governance.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The European Renaissance, characterized by a revival of classical Greek and Roman learning, humanism, and artistic mastery, began during the 14th century in:
options: Italian merchant city-states (such as Florence, Venice, and Genoa)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Renaissance origin ated in affluent northern Italian city-states (predominantly Florence under the Medici patronage) fueled by Mediterranean trade wealth, humanist philosophy (Petrarch), and artistic break throughs (Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Protestant Reform ation in 16th-century Europe was init i ated in 1517 when which German theologian nailed his Ninety-Five Theses criticizing papal indulgences to the church door in Wittenberg?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Martin Luther's Ninety-Five Theses (1517) denounced ecclesiastical corruption and papal sale of indulgences, sparking the Protestant Reform ation that fractured Western Christendom into Catholic and Protestant denominations.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The United States Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776, drafting Enlightenment principles of 'Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness', authored principally by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Thomas Jefferson penned the Declaration of Independence during the Second Continental Congress, drawing heavily from John Locke's social contract theory and natural rights philosophy.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Meiji Rest or ation of 1868 in Japan is historically famous for:
options: Isolating Japan completely from all global interaction for 300 years
Surrendering Japanese sovereignty to British colonial rule
Restoring practical imperial rule, abolishing the feudal Tokugawa Shogunate, and rapidly modernizing Japan into an industrial and military power
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Meiji Rest or ation dismantled the feudal samurai shogunate, modernized the economy, built modern industries, telegraphs, and railways, and reformed the military, enabling Japan to defeat Russia in 1905.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: At the Battle of Omdurman in 1898, British colonial forces under General Herbert Kitchener reconquered Sudan by defeating the armies of:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Kitchener utilized Maxim machine guns and gun boats at the Battle of Omdurman (September 1898) to defeat Khalifa Abdullah's Mahdist forces, establishing the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium over Sudan.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Maji Maji Rebel lion (1905–1907) was a massive armed anti-colonial up rising against forced cotton cultivation and brutal colonial tax ation in:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Spirit medium Kinjikitile Ngwale inspired diverse ethnic groups across German East Africa to unite against German colonial rule in the Maji Maji Rebel lion, resisting harsh labor exploitation.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The League of Nations failed to prevent the aggression of Fascist Italy against Ethiopia (1935) and Nazi Germany in Europe primarily because:
options: It possessed a massive standing international army that overwhelmed member states
It was controlled entirely by developing African nations
It met only once every fifty years
It lacked an independent armed enforcement mechanism and the United States never joined the organization
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The League of Nations was structurally weakened by the US Senate's refusal to ratify member ship, reliance on unanimous voting, and lack of military enforcement to stop Italian, German, and Japanese aggression.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Great Depression, the most severe global economic crisis of the 20th century, was triggered in October 1929 by:
options: The Wall Street stock market crash in the United States ('Black Tuesday')
The discovery of vast new gold mines in South Africa
The end of the Napoleonic Wars
The opening of the Panama Canal
