exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On October 29, 1929 ('Black Tuesday'), the New York Stock Exchange collapsed, leading to bank runs, industrial paralysis, hyper-unemployment, and a world wide economic depression throughout the 1930s.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), established following the 1955 Bandung Conference and 1961 Belgrade Summit, aimed to:
options: Merge all third-world nations into the Warsaw Pact under Soviet command
Enable developing Asian, African, and Latin American nations to maintain diplomatic neutrality and autonomy without aligning with either Cold War superpower bloc
Establish a single global monarchical government
Promote nuclear weapons proliferation among all member states
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Pioneered by leaders like Josip Broz Tito, Jawaharlal Nehru, Gamal Abdel Nasser, Kwame Nkrumah, and Sukarno, NAM sought self-determination, mutual non-aggression, and independence from US and Soviet Cold War spheres.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The October 1962 'Cuban Missile Crisis', which brought the world to the brink of direct thermonuclear war, occur red when the Soviet Union installed nuclear ballistic missiles in Cuba, confronting US President:
options: John F. Kennedy (confronting Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: For 13 days in October 1962, President John F. Kennedy instituted a naval quarantine of Cuba, resolving the crisis after Nikita Khrushchev agreed to with draw Soviet nuclear missiles in exchange for US pledges not to invade Cuba and remove US Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 historically symbolized:
options: The outbreak of World War I
The victory of the Ottoman Empire in Europe
The collapse of communist satellite regimes in Eastern Europe and the impending end of the Cold War division of Germany
The construction of the Iron Curtain
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On November 9, 1989, peaceful popular demonstrations led to the opening and demolition of the Berlin Wall, leading to German reunification in October 1990 and the unraveling of Soviet hegemony across Eastern Europe.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The African Union (AU) was officially launched in 2002 in Durban, South Africa, succeeding which earlier continental organization?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The African Union (AU) succeeded the OAU (1963–2002) to accelerate socio-economic and political continental integration under Agenda 2063, retaining its permanent head quarters in Addis Ababa.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The ancient trans-continental trade network that linked China, Central Asia, India, Pers i a, and the Mediterranean world for centuries is known as the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Silk Road was an over land network of trade routes origin ating during the Han Dynasty (c. 130 BCE) facilitating commerce in Chinese silk, paper, spices, porcelain, and cultural exchange across Eurasia.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Trans-Saharan Trade in medieval West and North Africa was fundamentally based on the exchange of which two vital primary commodities?
options: Gold (from West African forest mines) and Rock Salt (from Saharan deposits like Taghaza)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Camel caravans traversed the Sahara Desert exchanging gold and slaves from West Africa (Ghana, Mali, Songhai empires) for rock salt from Saharan mines, textiles, glassware, and Islamic scholarship.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The ancient Kingdom of Kush (Nubia), which once conquered and ruled Egypt as the 25th Pharaonic Dynasty, had its successive historical capitals at:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Kingdom of Kush developed along the Middle Nile in Sudan, shifting capitals from Kerma (c. 2500–1500 BCE) to Napata (c. 1000–300 BCE, under Piye and Taharqa), and finally to the iron-smelting center of Meroë (c. 300 BCE–350 CE).

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Kingdom of Aksum was the first sub-Saharan African state to mint its own indigenous coin age in gold, silver, and bronze, inscribed in which two languages?
options: Greek (for international trade) and Ge'ez (for domestic circulation)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Starting under King Endubis (c. 270 CE), Aksum minted coins bearing royal portraits and inscriptions in Greek (the lingua franca of Red Sea trade) and the indigenous Semitic Ge'ez script.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 14th-century Ethiopian epic and liturgical chronicle that established the national founding legend of the Queen of Sheba (Maked a) and King Solomon of Jerusalem is the:
options: Kebra Nagast ('The Glory of the Kings')
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Compiled under Nebura'ed Yeshaq of Axum in the early 14th century, the Kebra Nagast ('Glory of Kings') recounts the birth of Menelik I to Queen Maked a and King Solomon, the transfer of the Ark of the Covenant to Aksum, and divine legitimacy for the Solomonic dynasty.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: In 1622, which Ethiopian Emperor was convinced by Jesuit missionary Pedro Páez to convert to Roman Catholicism, provoking bloody religious civil wars across the highlands?
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Emperor Susenyos declared Catholicism the state religion in 1622 under Jesuit Patriarch Afonso Mendes, sparking nation wide religious rebel lions. Horrified by the blood shed, Susenyos abdicated in 1632 in favor of his son Fasilides, who restored Orthodox Christianity.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The 1882 Battle of Embabo in modern East Wollega was fought between King Menelik of Shewa and King Takla Haymanot of Gojjam for supremacy over:
options: Control of the rich southwestern trade routes and resources (coffee, ivory, gold)
The Red Sea port of Massawa
The coastal salt mines of Afar
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On June 6, 1882, Shewan forces under Menelik routed the Gojjame army under Takla Haymanot at Embabo, securing Shewan hegemony over the south west and prompting Emperor Yohannes IV to arbitrate regional spheres.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: King Menelik annexed the historic commercial and Islamic city-state of Harar in January 1887 following his victory over Emir Abdullahi at the:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On January 6, 1887, Menelik's army defeated Emir Abdullahi at Chelenqo, annexing the Emirate of Harar into the Ethiopian Empire and appointing his cousin Ras Makonnen Wolde Mikael as its governor.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: At the Battle of Dogali in January 1887, Ethiopian general Ras Alula Engida ('The Abba Nega') decisively defeated an invading Italian colonial battalion commanded by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On January 26, 1887, Ras Alula am bushed and wiped out a 500-man Italian column under Lt. Col. Tommaso De Cristoforis at Dogali near Massawa, in a major early victory against Italian colonial expansion.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: Following It aly's crushing defeat at the Battle of Adwa, the Treaty of Addis Ababa signed in October 1896 stipulated that:
options: Ethiopia would become an Italian protectorate
Italy unconditionally abrogated the Treaty of Wuchale and recognized the absolute sovereign independence of Ethiopia
Ethiopia agreed to pay war reparations to Rome
All Ethiopian ports were ceded to the Italian navy
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: The Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 26, 1896) nullified the Treaty of Wuchale, compelled Italy to recognize Ethiopia's unconditional sovereignty under international law, and established diplomatic relations between the two sovereign states.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The horrific 'Yekatit 12 Mass acre' (February 1937) was a three-day genocidal reprisal in Addis Ababa by Italian Fascist occupation forces under Viceroy Rodolfo Graziani following an assassin ation attempt by:
options: Abraha Deboch and Moges Asgedom (two young Eritrean-Ethiopian patriots)
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: On February 19, 1937 (Yekatit 12), Abraha Deboch and Moges Asgedom hurled grenades at Graziani at the Genete Le'ul palace. In retaliation, Fascist Black shirts murdered up to 30,000 civilians and mass acred the monks of Debre Libanos monastery.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Bale Peasant Rebel lion (1963–1970) was an armed agrarian revolt against imperial feudal land expropriation, religious marginalization, and unfair tax ation, led by:
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: General Waqo Gutu and guerrilla leaders in El Kere and Delo led pastoral and peasant populations of Bale in a seven-year armed rebel lion against land alien ation by absentee feudal land lords and high tax burdens.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The Gojjam Peasant Rebel lion of 1968 was provoked primarily by the imperial government's attempt to enforce:
options: Forced military conscription for foreign wars
A new Agricultural Income Tax Assessment system without local consent
The conversion of the population to Catholicism
The closure of all local markets
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: In 1968, Gojjam peasants revolted against government tax assess ors implementing the new Agricultural Income Tax Law, refusing tax payments until the imperial government suspended the tax and granted an amnesty.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: The selection of Addis Ababa as the permanent head quarters of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963 was largely due to:
options: The diplomatic prestige, continental leadership, and anti-colonial solidarity of Ethiopia and Emperor Haile Selassie I
Ethiopia offering the lowest rent for office spaces
A random lottery draw among all 32 founding delegates
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: Ethiopia's enduring symbol of African independence, Emperor Haile Selassie's mediation bridging the rival Casablanca and Monrovia blocs, and Ethiopia's active material backing for liberation movements earned Addis Ababa universal consensus as the diplomatic capital of Africa.

exam-2018-social-hist.text: What is the primary intellectual and societal significance of the rigorous, critical study of History?
options: To memorize isolated names and dates for competitive trivia games alone
To justify unverified myths and erase ancestral records
To cultivate national chauvinism and hostility toward neighboring states
To understand how past political, social, and economic processes have shaped the present, develop critical analytical skills, and foster informed civic responsibility
exam-2018-social-hist.explanation: History equips societies with critical thinking, evidence-based analysis, empathetic understanding of diverse human experiences, and causal insights into modern challenges to build a just and enlightened future.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following statements best defines the fundamental concept of 'Democracy' in modern political theory?
options: A system of government where supreme political authority is derived from the people through regular, free, fair, and competitive elections, governed by the rule of law and constitutional protection of fundamental human rights
An absolute monarchy where power is inherited perpetually within a single royal family
A military junta where policy decisions are decreed exclusively by senior armed forces officers
A totalitarian state where the ruling party prohibits all forms of political disagreement
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Democracy (derived from Greek 'demos' = people and 'kratos' = rule/power) is a system of governance where institutional power origin ates from citizen consent, exercised directly or through freely elected representatives under constitutional guarantees.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The principle of the 'Rule of Law' (Supremacy of Law) fundamentally means that:
options: Rulers and government officials are completely exempt from legal scrutiny and penalties
Laws can be arbitrarily created, modified, or suspended by executive orders without legislative approval
All persons, public institutions, and private entities—including the government itself—are accountable to publicly promulgated, equally enforced, and independently adjudicated laws
Only impoverished citizens must obey the penal code while wealthy individuals are above the law
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The Rule of Law establishes that no individual or state organ is above the law. Laws must be clear, public, stable, applied evenly, and administered by an independent judiciary.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In constitutional jurisprudence, 'Constitutionalism' refers to:
options: The unlimited expansion of military power over civil society
The political doctrine that the authority of government is derived from, defined by, and strictly limited by a body of fundamental law (the constitution)
The practice of rewriting the constitution whenever a new leader takes power
The total absence of any written legal framework in governance
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Constitutionalism is the political philosophy and institutional mechanism limiting government powers through entrenched legal constraints, preventing arbitrary tyranny and safe guarding fundamental liberties.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The political doctrine of 'Separation of Powers', famously articulated by French philosopher Baron de Montesquieu, divides state power into:
options: Ruling party, opposition parties, and non-voters
Armed forces, police, and private security companies
Three distinct branches: Legislative (law-making), Executive (law-enforcing), and Judicial (law-interpreting)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Separation of Powers allocates distinct governmental functions to three independent branches—the Legislature (makes statutory laws), Executive (implements laws), and Judiciary (interprets laws and resolves disputes)—preventing concentration of absolute power.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The institutional mechanism of 'Checks and Balances' functions to:
options: Enable each branch of government to monitor, constrain, and balance the powers of the other branches so that no single organ achieves unchecked dominance
Balance commercial bank accounts at the end of each fiscal month
Force the judiciary to obey executive orders without question
Eliminate the parliament in favor of a single supreme ruler
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Checks and Balances provides specific constitutional powers for branches to check each other (e.g., judicial review of laws, legislative impeachment/budget control, executive appointment vetos), maintaining institutional equilibrium.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Human rights are universally recognized as having which fundamental characteristics?
options: Temporary, negotiable, revocable at government convenience, and selective
Universal, inalienable, indivisible, interdependent, and inherent to all human beings without discrimination
Granted solely to citizens who have completed military service
Purchasable through private financial transactions in courts
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Human rights are inherent to all human beings regardless of nationality, race, gender, religion, or language; they are universal (belong to all), inalienable (cannot be taken away), and indivisible (all rights have equal moral standing).

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), the foundational corner stone of international human rights law, was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in Paris on:
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Adopted on December 10, 1948 by UN Resolution 217A (celebrated world wide as Human Rights Day), the UDHR articulates fundamental human rights in 30 articles to be universally protected.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following belongs to 'First-Generation Human Rights' (Civil and Political Rights)?
options: The right to life, freedom of expression, freedom of religion, right to fair trial, and right to vote
The right to clean running water and free university housing
The right to international planetary peace and technological transfers
The right to paid vacation and mandatory pensions
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: First-generation ('liberty-oriented' or negative) rights emerged from Enlightenment revolutions, protecting individuals from state tyranny (liberty, life, security of person, freedom of speech, assembly, voting, due process).

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Second-Generation Human Rights' (Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights) include:
options: The right to bear arms in civilian militias
The right to establish private monopolistic cartels
The right to unannounced warrantless wiretapping
The right to work, education, healthcare, an adequate standard of living, and social security
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Second-generation ('equality-oriented' or positive) rights require state action and progressive resource allocation to guarantee socio-economic well being (education, health care, fair wages, housing, cultural participation).

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Third-Generation Human Rights' (Solidarity / Group Rights) encompass which of the following?
options: The collective right to development, a healthy and clean environment, peace, and self-determination
The right to copyright private intellectual software
The right to establish political parties
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Third-generation (fraternity/solidarity) rights belong to groups and whole societies, focusing on global intergenerational issues: sustainable environment, peace, development, and self-determination.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: A 'Federal System of Government' (Federalism) is fundamentally characterized by:
options: The constitutional division of sovereign governing powers between a central federal authority and sub-national regional constituent states
A unitary system where all decisions are made in one central ministry
A direct military dictatorship with martial law
A confederation of independent nations with no central government
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Federalism combines shared rule for general purposes with regional self-rule for constituent units, balancing unity and diversity through a written constitution with protected jurisdictional spheres.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under the 1995 Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE), sovereign power in the nation resides in:
options: The Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples of Ethiopia (Article 8)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 8 of the FDRE Constitution explicitly declares: 'All sovereign power resides in the Nations, National i ties and Peoples of Ethiopia' and is expressed through their democratic representatives and direct democratic participation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Article 39 of the 1995 FDRE Constitution of Ethiopia guarantees:
options: The mandatory establishment of a state religion
The unconditional right of every Nation, Nationality, and People in Ethiopia to self-determination, including the right to secession
The prohibition of private property ownership
The lifetime appointment of the Prime Minister
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 39 guarantees every Nation, Nationality, and People the right to speak, write, and develop its language, promote its culture, self-govern within its territory, and exercise self-determination up to secession.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In Ethiopia's bicameral federal parliamentary structure, the highest authority of the Federal Government with legislative law-making powers is:
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 50 (3) and Article 55 of the FDRE Constitution establish the House of Peoples' Representatives (HPR, with members not exceeding 550 elected by universal suffrage for 5-year terms) as the highest authority of the Federal Government with legislative powers.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under the FDRE Constitution, which crucial constitutional responsibility is assigned to the House of Federation (HoF)?
options: Enacting the federal penal code and criminal statutes
Directing the armed forces in military combat
Interpreting the FDRE Constitution and determining the division of federal revenues/subsidies among regional states
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under Article 62, the House of Federation (composed of representatives of Nations, National i ties, and Peoples) is empowered to interpret the Constitution (assisted by the Council of Constitutional Inquiry), resolve inter-regional boundary disputes, and determine revenue-sharing formulas.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In the parliamentary system of the FDRE, who serves as the Chief Executive, Head of Government, and Commander-in-Chief of the National Armed Forces?
options: The Speaker of the House of Peoples' Representatives
The Chief Justice of the Federal Supreme Court
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under Article 72 and 74 of the FDRE Constitution, the Prime Minister is the Chief Executive, Head of Government, Chairman of the Council of Ministers, and Commander-in-Chief of the Ethiopian Armed Forces.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: What is the primary constitutional role of the President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia?
options: Commanding military tank divisions during active battles
Serving as Head of Government with complete executive decree powers
Serving as the ceremonial Head of State representing the nation and opening joint sessions of parliament
Drafting the annual federal economic budget
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under Article 69 and 71 of the Constitution, the President is the ceremonial Head of State of Ethiopia, elected in a joint session of the HPR and HoF for a six-year term, signing proclamations and accrediting ambassadors.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The independence of the judiciary is crucial in a democratic constitutional system because it ensures that:
options: Judges can adjudicate legal disputes and administer justice impartially, based strictly on facts and the law, free from political or external pressure
Courts can execute political dissidents without evidence
Judges are paid higher salaries than all private business owners
Court rulings can be overridden by police commanders at will
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Judicial independence (Article 78 & 79) guarantees that judges are subject only to the law and perform their duties without interference or influence from legislative, executive, or private interests.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Active 'Civic Participation' in a democratic society includes which of the following activities?
options: Vandalizing public infrastructure and avoiding all community dialogue
Exercising voting rights, engaging in peaceful public consultations, volunteering in community projects, and holding elected officials accountable
Bribing civil servants to bypass construction regulations
Spreading unverified defamatory rumors on digital platforms
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Civic participation is the voluntary involvement of citizens in democratic decision-making, policy dialogue, voting, community development initiatives, and civic over sight to improve public life.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Political Tolerance' is an essential democratic value defined as:
options: Suppression of all political groups that hold differing ideologies
Blindly agreeing with every government policy without questioning
The willingness to respect, accept, and protect the constitutional rights, freedoms, and lawful activities of individuals and groups whose political views differ from one's own
Encouraging violent clashes between political rivals
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Political tolerance requires recognizing and protecting the fundamental rights of political opponents, minor i ties, and dissenting voices to speak, organize, and campaign peacefully.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In a democratic multi-national state, true 'Democratic Patriotism' is best exemplified by:
options: Devotion to the wellbeing of one's country and fellow citizens, coupled with active commitment to constitutional principles, human rights, social justice, and constructive reform
Blind loyalty to political leaders regardless of corruption or illegality
Hostility, xenophobia, and aggression toward other ethnic or national communities
Complete indifference to national development and civic duties
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Democratic patriotism embraces national unity, mutual respect for cultural diversity, defense of constitutional rights, public service, and the moral courage to critique and correct injustice.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: How does 'Chauvinism' (hyper-nationalism) differ fundamentally from healthy democratic patriotism?
options: Chauvinism promotes international cooperation and human rights
Chauvinism values scientific education and civic literacy
Chauvinism respects ethnic and religious diversity
Chauvinism is an intolerant, aggressive, and uncritical belief in the innate superiority of one's own group over all others, fostering hostility and exclusion
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: While patriotism is love for one's country and democratic values without denigrating others, chauvinism represents an aggressive, supremacist, and exclusionary mind set that divides societies.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following is a primary hall mark of 'Ethical Leader ship' in public administration?
options: Using public office and state funds for personal family enrichment
Integrity, honesty, transparency, accountability, fairness, and unwavering dedication to the public interest
Suppressing whistleblowers who report financial fraud
Appointing unqualified relatives to key government positions
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Ethical leaders act with moral integrity, demonstrate openness, treat citizens equitably, safe guard public resources, and serve as ethical role models for the institutions they govern.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The term 'Corruption' is universally defined in governance and ethics as:
options: The abuse of entrusted public or private power, position, or authority for illicit personal, factional, or financial gain
The voluntary donation of personal income to charitable causes
The efficient and timely delivery of public services to citizens
The transparent public auditing of government financial accounts
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Corruption encompasses bribery, embezzlement, nepotism, extortion, and graft, diverting scarce public resources away from public services, distorting justice, and under mining public trust in institutions.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In Ethiopia, which specialized governmental institution was established to investigate, prevent, and prosecute corrupt practices and promote public integrity?
options: The Federal Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (FEACC)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The Federal Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (FEACC) was established by proclamation to combat corruption through public ethics education, institutional corruption risk assessments, and forensic investigations.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Transparency' in public administration requires that:
options: All government budgets and transactions be kept strictly secret from citizens
Governmental processes, public expenditures, official decisions, and policy rationales are openly accessible and understandable to the public and media
Public meetings be held in undisclosed locations behind locked doors
Public tenders and procurement contracts be awarded without open competitive bidding
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Transparency ensures that information regarding public expenditures, administrative rules, and state decisions is freely available, enabling scrutiny and deter ring corruption.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Account ability' in democratic governance means that:
options: Public officials and state organs must answer for their decisions, justify their expenditures, and accept legal and political consequences for their actions
Officials are permanently immune from parliamentary oversight
Citizens have no right to question administrative misconduct
State employees are only accountable to their immediate family members
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Account ability holds that power holders in government must be subject to over sight, regularly explain their conduct, and face sanctions if they abuse their authority or fail to deliver statutory man dates.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The constitutional principle of 'Due Process of Law' guarantees that:
options: Police may detain suspects indefinitely without bringing them before a judge
Citizens accused of crimes are denied legal defense representation
A court verdict can be pronounced without conducting a trial
No person can be deprived of life, liberty, or property without fair, established legal procedures and a fair, public trial by an impartial tribunal
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Due process of law (Article 19 & 20 of FDRE Constitution) ensures procedural fairness, including prompt not if i cat i on of charges, right to remain silent, legal represent ation, habeas corpus, and trial before an independent court.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The universal legal doctrine of the 'Presumption of Innocence' dictates that:
options: Anyone accused by a police officer is automatically guilty until proven innocent
Every person accused of a crime is presumed innocent until proven guilty according to law in a public trial with full defense guarantees
Criminal suspects must prove their innocence to avoid punishment
Only wealthy suspects are considered innocent
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Presumption of innocence places the legal burden of proof solely upon the prosecution to prove the defendant's guilt beyond reasonable doubt; the accused is considered innocent throughout the proceedings.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: An 'Institution of the Ombudsman' (Public Grievance Commissioner) is established to:
options: Receive, investigate, and rectify citizen complaints regarding administrative malpractice, injustice, corruption, or inefficiency in government ministries
Control the national electricity distribution grid
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman (EIO, established under Article 55 of the Constitution) investigates administrative injustices, bureaucratic errors, and abuses of discretion to protect citizen rights.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) is an independent constitutional organ whose statutory man date is to:
options: Collect import duties at maritime ports
Ensure that human rights and freedoms are respected, investigate human rights violations, and promote public human rights awareness
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The EHRC monitors human rights compliance across Ethiopia, visits prisons and detention centers, investigates alleged abuses, and issues independent recommend at i ons to state authorities.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The land mark Brundtland Commission Report (1987) defined 'Sustainable Development' as development that:
options: Meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Maximizes rapid industrial resource depletion without regard to environmental pollution
Relies entirely on perpetual foreign financial borrowing
Shuts down all modern economic production
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Sustainable development harmonizes three core dimensions: economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability, ensuring ecological resources are preserved for future generations.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Gender Equality' in civic and constitutional ethics means:
options: Denying education to girls in rural areas
Equal rights, responsibilities, opportunities, and fair treatment for women and men across political, economic, educational, and social spheres
Excluding women from holding political office and leadership positions
Paying women half the wages of male colleagues for the exact same work
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 35 of the FDRE Constitution affirms that women have equal rights with men in marital, political, social, and economic spheres, including equal rights to property ownership and equal pay for equal work.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Affirmative Action' measures are implemented in education and employment to:
options: Lower all educational standards across the board
Remedy historical injustices, systemic discrimination, and structural under-representation experienced by marginalized groups, such as women and historically disadvantaged communities
Abolish competitive merit-based grading systems entirely
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Affirmative action (Article 35 (3)) provides temporary remedial measures, preferential support, and training to enable historically marginalized groups to compete equitably in academia and public leader ship.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Why is active civic engagement in environmental conservation (such as tree planting and water shed management) a vital civic duty?
options: Because climate change, soil erosion, and biodiversity loss threaten national food security, public health, and ecological survival for present and future generations
Because it eliminates the need for modern agricultural equipment
Because trees can replace all municipal roads
Because environmental policies are irrelevant to national development
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Environmental protection preserves ecosystems, maintains fresh water sources, mitigates global warming, and protects agriculture, aligning with the constitutional right to a clean and healthy environment (Article 44).

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following describes an 'Alternative Dispute Resolution' (ADR) mechanism where a neutral third party facilitates dialogue between disputing parties to reach a mutually agreeable voluntary settlement?
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: In mediation, an impartial facilitator (med i at or) assists disputants in exploring options, communicating constructively, and reaching a collaborative, win-win settlement without formal court litigation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Traditional indigenous dispute resolution institutions in Ethiopia (such as Shimgelina, Guma, Jaarsummaa, Mada'a, and Xeer) are celebrated for:
options: Imposing high monetary court litigation fees
Restoring community harmony, reconciliation, and social peace through culturally respected elders and restorative justice principles
Delaying cases for several decades without resolution
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Ethiopia's traditional conflict resolution systems use community elders to facilitate dialogue, heal emotional trauma, repair social relations, and provide accessible, culturally rooted rest or ative justice.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Globalization' refers to the multidimensional historical process characterized by:
options: The complete isolation of all sovereign nation states from one another
The abolition of all global international telecommunications
The increasing worldwide interconnectedness, integration, and interdependence of national economies, technologies, trade, cultures, and governance
The closure of all international airports and shipping corridors
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Globalization expands cross-border flows of goods, services, capital, digital information, and cultural exchanges, creating economic opportunities while posing challenges for local cultural preservation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: A positive 'Work Ethic' in personal and professional development is demonstrated by:
options: Punctuality, diligence, responsibility, professional integrity, continuous self-improvement, and pride in productive labor
Arriving late, avoiding difficult tasks, and blaming colleagues for errors
Expecting monetary wages without performing assigned job duties
Taking credit for the intellectual achievements of other team members
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: A strong work ethic reflects commitment, reliability, moral integrity, crafts man ship, discipline, and personal responsibility, which are essential drivers of personal productivity and national economic progress.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Developing a habit of 'Saving' and financial prudence is essential for individuals and nations because:
options: It eliminates all forms of physical currency from circulation
It accumulates domestic financial capital, provides a financial safety net for emergencies, and funds productive investments in infrastructure and industry
It forces people to stop consuming necessary nutritious food
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Saving mobilizes domestic capital for industrial investments, cushions house holds against unexpected economic shocks, and reduces reliance on foreign borrowing.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Self-Reliance' at both individual and national levels is defined as:
options: Refusing to engage in any international diplomacy or trade
Complete isolation from world scientific discoveries
Relying on perpetual external food hand-outs and foreign debt
Relying principally on one's own internal capabilities, resources, hard work, and ingenuity to achieve sustainable growth and independence
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Self-reliance builds auto no my and dignity by mobilizing domestic labor, technology, and natural resources to meet national development priorities without becoming subservient to external dependency.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Critical Thinking' in civic education enables citizens to:
options: Objectively analyze evidence, evaluate arguments, detect biases and logical fallacies, and make reasoned, informed civic decisions
Blindly accept unverified rumors on social media as absolute truth
Reject scientific consensus in favor of conspiracy theories
Obey political authority without any rational evaluation
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Critical thinking is an essential civic competency that safe guards democratic societies from propaganda, manipulation, and polarization through evidence-based, rational inquiry.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In a democratic multi-cultural society, 'Pluralism' is best understood as:
options: The forced cultural assimilation of all minority cultures into one single identity
The complete prohibition of all non-governmental organizations
The peaceful, recognized coexistence of diverse ethnic, cultural, religious, and political groups and perspectives within a unified constitutional society
The expulsion of non-native residents from municipal cities
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Pluralism affirms that diversity of opinions, cultures, beliefs, and political associations enriches democratic society and must be protected through constitutional rights and mutual respect.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The civic concept of 'Social Justice' is fundamentally concerned with:
options: Promoting extreme wealth concentration among a small ruling elite
The fair and equitable distribution of opportunities, resources, rights, and privileges across all strata of society, preventing structural marginalization
Eliminating all courts and judicial legal systems
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Social justice strives for a fair society where all individuals enjoy equal life chances, basic social security, non-discrimination, and protection from systemic exploitation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: What is the crucial distinction between 'Equality ' and ' Equity'?
options: Equality provides everyone with the exact same resources, while Equity allocates resources tailored to specific needs and systemic barriers to achieve fair outcomes
Equality is illegal while Equity is legal
Equality applies only to corporate finance while Equity applies to mathematics
Equality means giving more to the rich while Equity means giving nothing to anyone
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: While equality treats everyone identically regardless of starting point, equity recognizes historical inequalities and provides proportional resources (e.g., affirmative action, targeted health care) to ensure genuine fairness.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The principle of 'Unity in Diversity' in Ethiopia emphasizes:
options: Erasing all unique languages and distinct regional cultural traditions
Creating separate independent nation-states for every single language group
Fostering common national citizenship, shared constitutional values, and solidarity while celebrating and respecting linguistic, cultural, and religious diversity
Suppressing public cultural festivals and heritage celebrations
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Unity in Diversity builds a cohesive nation bound by shared democratic institutions and collective economic interests, while protecting and developing the unique her it age and self-determination of all communities.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In public economics and governance, 'Public Goods' (such as national defense, street lighting, public high ways, and flood control dykes) are distinguished by being:
options: Sold exclusively to private luxury resort owners
Excludable and highly rivalrous in consumption
Manufactured only by foreign military contractors
Non-excludable (available to all citizens) and non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce availability to others)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Public goods exhibit non-excludability (no one can be bar red from using them) and non-rivalry (consumption by one does not deplete the good for others), necessitating public government funding through tax ation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Paying taxes honestly and promptly is an indispensable civic duty because:
options: Taxes generate public revenue required to construct schools, hospitals, roads, generate clean energy, maintain security, and deliver essential public services
Taxes are designed solely to enrich private bank owners
Taxes are only collected during wartime
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Tax ation provides the financial found ation for public infrastructure, social safety nets, education, health care, and state administration. Tax evasion under mines the delivery of vital public services.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: International Humanitarian Law (the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and Additional Protocols) establishes legal rules during armed conflict to:
options: Encourage unrestricted destruction of civilian hospitals and schools
Protect wounded combatants, prisoners of war, medical personnel, and non-combatant civilian populations, restricting methods and means of warfare
Legalize biological and chemical warfare against civilians
Abolish the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: International Humanitarian Law (IHL / laws of armed conflict) limits the effects of armed conflict by protecting civilians, medics, and captured soldiers, and out lawing indiscriminate weapons and torture.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) contribute to democratic governance by:
options: Declaring states of emergency in regional parliaments
Advocating for citizen rights, delivering humanitarian aid, promoting civic education, and monitoring government policy and human rights compliance
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Civil society acts as an essential intermediary between the state and the individual, articulating community concerns, advancing human rights, building social capital, and holding institutions accountable.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: What is the primary operational difference between 'Direct Democracy ' and ' Represent ative Democracy'?
options: In direct democracy, citizens vote directly on legislation and public policies (as in referendums), whereas in representative democracy, citizens elect delegates to make laws on their behalf
Direct democracy has no elections while representative democracy has no constitution
Representative democracy is only practiced in monarchies
Direct democracy prohibits all citizen participation
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: In direct democracy (ancient A thens, town hall meetings, referendums), citizens debate and vote on laws themselves; in represent ative democracy (modern republics and parliaments), citizens choose elected officials to govern.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following conditions is indispensable for an election to be considered 'Free and Fair'?
options: Banning opposition political parties from registering candidates
Allowing the ruling party to count votes without independent observers
Intimidating voters with armed police inside polling booths
Universal adult franchise, secret ballot, impartial electoral administration, equal campaign access, and freedom from intimidation
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Free and fair elections require universal suffrage, secret voting booths, an independent electoral board (NEBE), fair media access, peaceful campaigning, and transparent vote counting.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) is legally established as:
options: A partisan committee of the ruling political party
An autonomous, independent constitutional institution responsible for conducting federal, regional, and municipal elections and administering political party registrations
A division of the Ministry of Defense
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under Article 102 of the FDRE Constitution and establishing proclamations, the NEBE operates independently from political control to conduct free, fair, and transparent democratic elections.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'State Sovereignty' in international relations refers to:
options: The supreme, absolute, and independent legal authority of a state to govern its territory and population without external interference
The subordination of developing nations to foreign superpowers
The right of a neighboring nation to unilaterally redraw international borders
The absence of any domestic police force
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Sovereignty (recognized in UN Charter Article 2 (1)) denotes internal supremacy over domestic jurisdiction and external independence from foreign control.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The democratic doctrine of 'Popular Sovereignty' implies that:
options: Government officials derive their legitimacy solely from hereditary descent
The military possesses inherent right to govern without civilian oversight
The ultimate source of all political authority and governing legitimacy is the will of the people
Foreign ambassadors decide national domestic policies
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Popular sovereignty holds that government is created by and subject to the will of the people, who delegate limited authority to elected representatives.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The democratic standard of 'Majority Rule with Minority Rights' ensures that:
options: The electoral majority can eliminate all human rights of minority populations
Decisions are made by majority vote, while constitutional safeguards protect the fundamental rights and liberties of minorities from being infringed
Minority groups are prohibited from voting in national elections
Elections are decided by the smallest minority faction
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Majoritarian democracy must be bounded by constitutional rights; while the majority forms government and passes laws, it cannot a bridge the equal protection, language, religious, or speech rights of minor i ties.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The fundamental right to 'Freedom of Expression' (Article 29 of FDRE Constitution) includes:
options: The right to seek, receive, and impart information and ideas of all kinds through speech, print, digital media, or artistic forms without censorship
The right to defame individuals with deliberately fabricated falsehoods
The right to broadcast hate speech inciting ethnic violence
The right to disclose classified military state secrets during wartime
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 29 protects freedom of thought, opinion, and expression, including press freedom and the prohibition of any form of state censor ship, which are essential for informed democratic discourse.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under democratic constitutional law, lawful restrict i ons may be placed on freedom of expression only when speech:
options: Criticizes a government economic policy peacefully
Exposes administrative corruption in a municipality
Expresses support for an opposition political party
Directly incites war, ethnic hatred, imminent violence, defamation, or threatens public health and safety
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under international law and Article 29 (6), freedom of expression carries civic responsibilities and can be constitutionally limited by laws protecting individual dignity, public order, and prohibiting hate speech or war propaganda.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The constitutional principle of 'Freedom of Religion and Belief' (Article 27 of FDRE Constitution) guarantees that:
options: The federal government establishes one official compulsory national religion
Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion, including the freedom to hold or adopt a religion or belief of their choice
Religious groups are prohibited from building places of worship
Citizens can be forced to convert to a specific faith to obtain employment
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 27 affirms that everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience, and religion, including the freedom to worship individually or in community, in public or private, without state interference.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under Article 11 of the FDRE Constitution, the principle of 'Secularism' (Separation of State and Religion) man dates that:
options: State and religion are separate; there is no state religion; and the state shall not interfere in religious matters, nor religion in state affairs
The government must fund all religious pilgrimages equally
Religious leaders must serve as cabinet ministers
Religious education is compulsory in all public secular universities
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 11 enshrines state secularism: (1) State and religion are separate; (2) There shall be no state religion; (3) The state shall not interfere in religious affairs and religion shall not interfere in state affairs.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and Article 36 of the FDRE Constitution, in all actions concerning children, the primary consideration shall be:
options: The best interests of the child
Enrolling all children in military academies
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 36 (2) explicitly provides: 'In all actions concerning children under taken by public and private welfare institutions, courts of law, administrative authorities or legislative bodies, the primary consideration shall be the best interests of the child.'

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The human rights of Persons with Disabilities require society and state institutions to:
options: Institutionalize them permanently in isolated facilities
Ensure reasonable accommodation, accessible public infrastructure, inclusive quality education, and equal employment opportunities free from discrimination
Deny them national identification cards and voting rights
Prohibit them from participating in sporting events
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) man dates full accessibility, non-discrimination, inclusive education, and equal participation in social, economic, and political life.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In the Ethiopian legal system, the statutory enactments passed by the House of Peoples' Representatives are officially termed:
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under Ethiopian law, the House of Peoples ' Representatives passes primary legislation termed ' Proclamations'; the Council of Ministers issues 'Regulations'; and individual ministries issue 'Directives'.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In the hierarchy of Ethiopian legal norms, which law is the supreme law of the land, rendering any law, customary practice, or decision of a state organ null and void if it contravenes it?
options: The Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (Article 9)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Article 9 (1) of the FDRE Constitution establishes Constitutional Supremacy: 'The Constitution is the supreme law of the land. Any law, customary practice or a decision of an organ of state or a public official which contravenes this Constitution shall be of no effect.'

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The legal Latin phrase 'Ultra Vires' refers to actions taken by an administrative body or government official that:
options: Are completely in accordance with constitutional authority
Exceed the lawful scope of powers conferred upon them by statutory law, making such actions legally invalid and void
Have been approved by a two-thirds majority in parliament
Are performed by private military contractors abroad
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: 'Ultra Vires' ('beyond the powers') applies when a public official or administrative agency acts outside the legal limits set by the constitution or enabling legislation, rendering the act void.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: What is the primary difference between a 'Civic Duty' (mandatory legal obligation) and a 'Civic Responsibility' (voluntary moral practice)?
options: A civic duty is legally enforceable with penalties for non-compliance (e.g., paying taxes, obeying laws, jury service), whereas a civic responsibility is socially and morally encouraged (e.g., voting, volunteering, community dialogue)
Civic duties are optional while civic responsibilities are illegal
Civic duties apply only to foreign tourists
There is no difference whatsoever between them
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Duties (such as respecting the constitution, paying taxes, testifying in court when summoned) are legally man dated; responsibilities (participating in civil society, voting, cleaning public spaces) reflect active civic virtue.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Traditional community self-help institutions in Ethiopia, such as 'Iddir' (burial mutual aid) and 'Equb' (rotating credit association), are vital social institutions because they:
options: Collect federal customs tariffs at border checkpoints
Provide grassroots social security, financial mutual assistance, crisis support, and foster enduring community solidarity
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Iddir and Equb represent indigenous social capital and financial cooperation, providing essential community safety nets, insurance against grief/loss, and informal microfinance without bureaucratic hurdles.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Whistleblower Protection' laws are enacted in anti-corruption legislation to:
options: Arrest journalists who report on public health
Protect and shield ethical employees and citizens who report corruption, financial embezzlement, and illegal wrongdoing within institutions from retaliation, dismissal, or threats
Reward corporate cartels who fix commodity prices
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Whistleblower protections encourage reporting of fraud, waste, and corruption by legally shielding informants from work place harassment, term ination, and physical retaliation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The unethical administrative practice of appointing or favoring unqualified relatives and family members to public offices and procurement contracts is termed:
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Nepotism is a form of corruption where officials abuse their authority to grant public appointments, promotions, or lucrative contracts to family members, violating the principles of fairness and merit.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: A genuine 'Meritocracy' in civil service recruitment and promotion ensures that:
options: Jobs are inherited from parents to children automatically
Appointments are sold to the highest bidder
Employment is restricted to members of a single political party
Individuals are evaluated, selected, and promoted based objectively on their demonstrated competence, skills, educational credentials, and professional excellence
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Meritocracy creates an efficient, fair, and professional civil service by selecting talent based on standardized qualifications, competitive exams, and demonstrated performance rather than nepotism or political patronage.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Professional Ethics' refers to:
options: The formalized codes of moral standards, ethical duties, and behavioral guidelines governing the conduct of professionals (such as doctors, lawyers, engineers, and teachers)
Maximizing corporate profits by violating safety regulations
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Professional ethics (e.g., medical Hippocratic Oath, legal ethics) regulates professional conduct, requiring competence, integrity, confidentiality, and commitment to public welfare above personal interest.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Moral Courage' in civic leader ship and citizenship is demonstrated when an individual:
options: Stands up for ethical principles, human rights, and the truth despite facing personal risk, peer pressure, political intimidation, or social disapproval
Follows the corrupt crowd to avoid conflict
Takes bribes secretly while pretending to be honest in public
Abuses vulnerable citizens when no one is looking
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Moral courage is the willingness to up hold ethical standards, defend victims of injustice, and speak truth to power, even when doing so entails personal hard ship, loss of status, or danger.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In civic theory, how does an 'Active Citizen ' differ from a ' Passive Citizen'?
options: Active citizens commit criminal offenses while passive citizens work in banks
Passive citizens run for parliament while active citizens avoid voting
Active citizens proactively participate in community affairs, volunteer, vote, and advocate for positive social change, whereas passive citizens merely obey laws without engaging in civic life
Active citizens are all civil engineers
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Active citizenship involves proactive civic engagement, community leader ship, informed voting, and public problem-solving, whereas passive citizenship is limited to basic obedience to laws.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Digital Citizenship' encompasses:
options: Spreading malware and hacking municipal water grids
The responsible, ethical, safe, and respectful use of technology, digital information, and social media platforms
Creating fake identities to bully students online
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Digital citizenship involves digital literacy, on line privacy protection, evaluating information credibility, avoiding cyberbullying, and using internet technologies constructively.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following on line behaviors constitutes a serious violation of cyber ethics and cyber law?
options: Cyberbullying, identity theft, unauthorized system hacking, phishing, and deliberately spreading toxic disinformation
Submitting homework through a secure school portal
Sending polite email queries to university professors
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Cybercrimes—such as hacking, phishing scams, spreading hate speech, identity theft, and on line defamation—harm individuals, disrupt digital infrastructure, and carry severe legal penalties.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The phenomenon of 'Brain Drain' refers to:
options: The complete loss of memory due to neurological illness
The reduction of school hours during vacation periods
The purchase of imported scientific calculators
The mass emigration of highly educated, skilled, and trained professionals (doctors, engineers, professors) from developing nations to affluent countries in search of higher pay and better conditions
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Brain drain deprives developing countries of critical human capital (such as physicians and engineers) trained at public expense, hindering national economic and health care development.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Dependency Syndrome' is a psychological and socio-economic condition where:
options: A community becomes completely self-sufficient and stops importing luxury goods
Individuals or communities lose self-initiative and become perpetually reliant on government hand-outs and foreign food aid rather than working for sustainable self-reliance
A nation manufactures all its own industrial equipment
Citizens invest heavily in national treasury bonds
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Dependency syndrome under mines community self-initiative and resilience by fostering reliance on perpetual external hand outs rather than productive labor and local problem solving.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Ethiopia 's ' Green Legacy Init i ative' is an ambitious national project designed to:
options: Combating deforestation, soil degradation, and desertification by planting billions of seedlings across Ethiopia to enhance forest cover and food security
Replacing all traditional coffee farms with concrete parking lots
Selling all national forests to multinational timber corporations
Painting all government buildings in green color
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Launched in 2019, the Green Legacy Init i ative mobilizes millions of citizens to plant billions of indigenous, fruit, and agro-forestry trees annually to restore degraded ecosystems, mitigate climate change, and bolster food security.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The construction of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on the Abay (Blue Nile) River embodies the international legal principle of:
options: Unilateral monopolization of river waters without generating power
Equitable and reasonable utilization of transboundary watercourses without causing significant harm to downstream nations
Prohibiting any regional energy integration with neighboring states
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Under international water law (UN Water courses Convention), GERD exemplifies equitable and reasonable utilization by generating clean renewable hydroelectricity for development while maintaining river flows without causing significant harm to downstream riparians.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Under the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 'Diplomatic Immunity' grants accredited diplomats:
options: Protection from arrest, prosecution, and civil litigation in the receiving host country to ensure they can discharge their official diplomatic functions without coercion
The right to commit violent crimes with total exemption from international law
The authority to rewrite the constitution of the host nation
The right to own all local mineral mines in the host territory
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Diplomatic immunity protects accredited diplomats from host country arrest, detention, or prosecution, ensuring sovereign states can conduct foreign policy and dialogue without harassment or host age taking.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The formal legal process through which one sovereign country surrenders a suspected or convicted criminal to another country for prosecution or punishment is known as:
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Extra dition is regulated by bilateral treat ies and international agreements, enabling sovereign governments to transfer criminal suspects across borders to face justice in the jurisdiction where the offense was committed.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Regional economic integration bodies in Africa (such as IGAD, COMES A, EAC, and ECOWAS) strive to:
options: Increase prohibitive tariff barriers among neighboring countries
Prohibit all movement of goods and cross-border transport
Eliminate trade barriers, promote economic cooperation, improve regional infrastructure, and harmonize market policies
Impose economic sanctions on member states
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Regional economic communities (RECs) serve as the building blocks for continental integration, lowering customs tariffs, connecting power grids and high ways, and expanding regional commerce.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), head quartered in Accra, Ghana, was created to:
options: Create a single continental free trade market for goods and services across 54 African nations, boosting intra-African trade and industrialization
Impose European manufactured goods across Africa without tariffs
Abolish all African national central banks
Restrict African products from entering African markets
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: AfCFTA creates the largest free trade area in the world by number of member countries, reducing tariffs on 90% of goods to expand intra-African trade, industrialization, and continental supply chains.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), adopted in 2015 as the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, comprise how many interconnected global goals?
options: 17 goals (including No Poverty, Zero Hunger, Quality Education, and Climate Action)
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The 17 SDGs encompass comprehensive targets for ending poverty, protecting the biosphere, improving education and health care, achieving gender equality, and fostering global partnership by 2030.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Which of the following is considered a core dimension of the Rule of Law Index compiled by global governance institutions?
options: The number of military tanks on display in national parades
Absence of corruption, fundamental human rights protections, open and transparent government, order and security, and accessible civil and criminal justice
The height of municipal skyscraper buildings
The total quantity of imported luxury motor vehicles
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The Rule of Law Index (World Justice Project) evaluates legal systems across 8 factors: constraints on government powers, absence of corruption, open government, fundamental rights, order/security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice, and criminal justice.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The ancient constitutional writ of 'Habeas Corpus' protects citizens by:
options: Requiring that a person who has been arrested or detained be brought before a court of law without delay so the judge can determine the legality of the detention
Authorizing the indefinite secret detention of citizens without trial
Requiring all citizens to pay court fees in gold bullion
Allowing police to confiscate private property without warrants
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Habeas corpus ('you shall have the body') is a corner stone protection against arbitrary detention, requiring authorities to present the prisoner to a court and demonstrate lawful just if i cat i on for detention.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The unethical political practice known as 'Gerrymandering' involves:
options: Promoting women candidates in democratic elections
Conducting an accurate national census every ten years
Redrawing the geographic boundaries of electoral voting districts to give an unfair partisan advantage to a particular political party
Installing electronic voting machines in rural communities
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Gerrymandering manipulates district boundary lines to pack or crack opposing voters, distorting electoral represent ation and under mining competitive democracy.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Civil Disobedience' (advocated by Henry David Thoreau, Mahatma Gandhi, and Martin Luther King Jr.) is characterized as:
options: Armed terrorism aimed at overthrowing the state violently
The deliberate, public, non-violent refusal to obey an unjust law or policy, accepting legal penalties to appeal to the moral conscience of society and effect reform
Secretly committing petty theft at night
Refusing to attend secondary school classes
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Civil disobedience is nonviolent, principled, public resistance against unjust laws, where protesters accept legal consequences to expose systemic injustice and mobilize democratic change.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Social Cohesion' in a multi-ethnic community is strengthened when:
options: There is mutual trust, shared civic values, equality of opportunity, social inclusion, and active cross-cultural solidarity
Communities live in segregated, hostile enclaves
Certain cultural groups are denied basic healthcare and schooling
Ethnic stereotyping and derogatory slurs are promoted in media
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Social cohesion reflects the strength of social bonds, mutual respect, shared civic pride, and trust among diverse citizens, preventing social fragment ation and conflict.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Xenophobia' is an irrational and harmful social prejudice defined as:
options: The fear of high mountain peaks
The scientific study of foreign plant species
The celebration of international cultural festivals
The deep-rooted hatred, fear, prejudice, or discrimination directed against foreigners, immigrants, or people perceived as outsiders
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Xenophobia manifests in hostility, exclusion, and violence against immigrants and refugees, violating universal human rights and under mining global peace and solidarity.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In ethical philosophy, 'Altruism' refers to:
options: Relentless pursuit of self-interest at the expense of others
Unselfish concern, empathy, and active devotion to the wellbeing, happiness, and service of others without expecting personal gain or reward
Hoarding scarce resources during an emergency
Refusing to cooperate with community members
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Altruism is the moral virtue of selfless service to others, inspiring volunteering, disaster relief, philanthropy, and community solidarity.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: Universal access to quality 'Primary Education' is recognized as a fundamental human right because:
options: It empowers individuals with literacy, critical thinking, economic productivity, civic awareness, and breaks the intergenerational cycle of poverty
It forces everyone to choose the same career path
It only benefits the industrial banking sector
It prevents citizens from understanding their legal rights
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Education is an empowering human right that enhances personal dignity, health literacy, civic participation, gender empowerment, and national economic development.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Intellectual Property Rights' (patents, copyrights, and trade marks) are legally protected to:
options: Prohibit authors from publishing any books
Prevent scientific innovations from ever being used in medicine
Encourage creativity and innovation by granting creators and inventors legal protections and economic rewards for their original intellectual creations
Allow competitors to freely pirate original software without consequences
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Intellectual property laws protect invent ors, authors, and artists from theft and unauthorized copying, fostering incentives for research, development, artistic creativity, and technological innovation.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), 'Food Security' exists when:
options: A country imports all its basic food crops from abroad
All people, at all times, have physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life
Food is available only to military officers
All traditional farms are converted into urban shopping plazas
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Food security rests on four pillars: availability (sufficient quantity), access (economic/physical ability to obtain food), utilization (nutritional value and safe water), and stability over time.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Rest or ative Justice' focuses on:
options: Repairing the harm caused by criminal behavior, promoting healing and reconciliation among the victim, the offender, and the affected community
Inflicting the maximum physical pain on convicted offenders
Executing all accused individuals without trial
Ignoring the needs and feelings of crime victims
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Rest or ative justice views crime as a violation of people and relationships, emphasizing offender account ability, restitution to the victim, and community reintegration.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: In contrast to rest or ative justice, 'Retributive Justice' is guided by the principle that:
options: Offenders should receive rehabilitation and job training exclusively
Criminals should never face any legal sanctions
Punishment should be inflicted on wrongdoers strictly in proportion to the severity of the crime committed ('just deserts')
Victims should be punished for reporting crimes
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Retributive justice holds that offenders morally deserve proportionate punishment for their transgressions according to established penal law, restoring moral balance.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Distributive Justice' in political and moral philosophy addresses:
options: The military conquest of foreign lands
The fair, ethical, and equitable allocation of economic benefits, public resources, social opportunities, and tax burdens across a society
The distribution of weapons to private militias
The closure of rural transportation links
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Distributive justice (explored by John Rawls and Aristotle) concerns moral principles governing the fair allocation of social goods, wealth, public services, and tax ation burdens.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: 'Procedural Justice' requires that:
options: The legal and administrative processes and rules used to make decisions are transparent, fair, unbiased, consistent, and respectful of all participants' rights
Court judges decide cases based on bribery payments
The outcome of every trial is predetermined by the executive branch
Rules are changed retroactively during the middle of a trial
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Procedural justice focuses on the fairness of the dispute resolution process itself—giving all parties a voice, treating people with dignity, neutrality, and clear rules.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: According to the United Nations Development Program me (UNDP), which of the following represents a comprehensive set of characteristics defining 'Good Governance'?
options: Censorship, judicial bias, nepotism, and inequality
High inflation, unemployment, and lack of accountability
Participation, Rule of Law, Transparency, Responsiveness, Consensus Orientation, Equity and Inclusiveness, Effectiveness and Efficiency, and Accountability
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: The UNDP identifies eight major characteristics of good governance: participatory, rule of law, transparent, responsive, consensus-oriented, equitable and inclusive, effective and efficient, and accountable.

exam-2018-social-civics.text: The ultimate over arching objective of Civics and Ethical Education in secondary schools is to:
options: Cultivate informed, virtuous, active, critically thinking, and patriotic citizens committed to democracy, the rule of law, human rights, and national development
Train students exclusively in memorizing historical dates without understanding
Discourage young citizens from participating in community volunteer work
Promote ethnic prejudice and social intolerance among youth
exam-2018-social-civics.explanation: Civics and Ethical Education equips students with moral values, democratic principles, legal awareness, critical thinking, and civic responsibilities to become productive, ethical leaders and active participants in building a democratic and prosperous society.

exam-2018-social-econ.text: The fundamental economic problem that forms the found ation of all economic inquiry across all human societies is:
options: The scarcity of productive economic resources relative to unlimited human wants and needs
The overproduction of luxury manufactured consumer goods
The complete absence of physical paper currency in commercial banks
The existence of international maritime shipping tariffs
exam-2018-social-econ.explanation: Scarcity is the universal condition that human wants and desires exceed the finite productive resources (land, labor, capital, entrepreneur ship) available to satisfy them, necessitating choice and allocation.

exam-2018-social-econ.text: The concept of 'Opportunity Cost' is scientific ally defined in economic decision-making as:
options: The total monetary cash paid for purchasing a new commercial product
The accounting profit recorded on a corporate balance sheet
The value of the next best alternative that is forgone or sacrificed when making a choice
The average historical cost of raw material inputs
exam-2018-social-econ.explanation: Opportunity cost measures the real economic cost of any decision by evaluating the highest-valued for gone alternative (e.g., studying for an exam rather than earning wages at work).

exam-2018-social-econ.text: On a Production Possibility Curve (PPC / PPF), an economic out put combination that lies strictly inside the frontier curve sign if ies:
options: An unattainable production level with current technology
Inefficient production characterized by unemployment, underemployment, or misallocation of available economic resources
A state of hyper-inflation in the national economy
exam-2018-social-econ.explanation: Points on the PPC represent productive efficiency (full employment); points inside indicate idle resources or inefficient allocation; points outside are currently unattainable without economic growth or technological progress.

exam-2018-social-econ.text: The 'Law of Demand' states that, holding all other factors constant (ceteris paribus):
options: There is an inverse (negative) relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded of that good
As the price of a good rises, consumers will buy more of that good
Price changes have no effect on consumer purchasing volume
Higher consumer income always reduces quantity demanded
exam-2018-social-econ.explanation: Under the Law of Demand (ceteris paribus), as price ($P$) increases, quantity demanded ($Q_d$) decreases, and as price falls, quantity demanded rises due to substitution and income effects.

exam-2018-social-econ.text: The 'Law of Supply' states that, ceteris paribus:
options: Producers supply less when the market price rises
Supply is determined entirely by consumer preferences
Price and quantity supplied are inversely related
There is a direct (positive) relationship between the price of a good and the quantity producers are willing and able to supply to the market
exam-2018-social-econ.explanation: Because higher market prices incentivize higher profit margins, producers increase the quantity supplied ($Q_s$) when price ($P$) increases, yielding an upward-sloping supply curve.

exam-2018-social-econ.text: In a competitive free market, 'Market Equilibrium' occurs at the unique price point where:
options: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied creating a perpetual shortage
